   189	variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R] {M : Type v} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
   190	
   191	/-- **The `lm:ctn`-lite slicing criterion, endomorphism form** (Kleiman `lm:ctn`
   192	(iii)⟹(i), Tor-free; DAT-A2 core): over a Noetherian ring `R`, an `R`-linear
   193	endomorphism of a flat module that is injective on every residue-field fibre is
   194	injective. Noetherian induction on ideals with `P I := ∀ x, φ x ∈ I•⊤ → x ∈ I•⊤`; the
   195	fibre hypothesis fires at the primes, the flat colon lemma splices the non-primes. -/
   196	theorem Module.Flat.injective_of_forall_rTensor_residueField_injective
   197	    [IsNoetherianRing R] [Module.Flat R M] (φ : M →ₗ[R] M)
   198	    (hfib : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum R,
   199	      Function.Injective (φ.rTensor p.asIdeal.ResidueField)) :
   200	    Function.Injective φ := by
   201	  have key : ∀ I : Ideal R, ∀ x : M,
   202	      φ x ∈ I • (⊤ : Submodule R M) → x ∈ I • (⊤ : Submodule R M) := by
   203	    intro I₀
   204	    refine IsNoetherian.induction
   205	      (P := fun I : Ideal R => ∀ x : M,
   206	        φ x ∈ I • (⊤ : Submodule R M) → x ∈ I • (⊤ : Submodule R M))
   207	      (fun I IH => ?_) I₀
   208	    intro x hx
   209	    by_cases htop : I = ⊤
   210	    · rw [htop, Submodule.top_smul]
   211	      exact Submodule.mem_top
   212	    by_cases hp : Ideal.IsPrime I
   213	    · -- the prime case: the fibre hypothesis, no inductive hypothesis
   214	      haveI := hp
   215	      have h1 : (φ.rTensor (Ideal.ResidueField I))
   216	          (x ⊗ₜ[R] (1 : Ideal.ResidueField I)) = 0 := by
   217	        rw [LinearMap.rTensor_tmul]
   218	        exact tmul_residueField_one_eq_zero_of_mem_smul_top I hx
   219	      have h2 : (x ⊗ₜ[R] (1 : Ideal.ResidueField I) :
   220	          M ⊗[R] Ideal.ResidueField I) = 0 :=
   221	        hfib ⟨I, hp⟩ (by rw [h1, map_zero] :
   222	          (φ.rTensor (Ideal.ResidueField I)) (x ⊗ₜ[R] (1 : Ideal.ResidueField I)) =
   223	            (φ.rTensor (Ideal.ResidueField I)) 0)
   224	      exact Module.Flat.mem_smul_top_of_tmul_residueField_one_eq_zero I h2
   225	    · -- the non-prime case: splice two strictly larger ideals
   226	      obtain ⟨a, b, hab, ha, hb⟩ : ∃ a b : R, a * b ∈ I ∧ a ∉ I ∧ b ∉ I := by
   227	        by_contra hcon
   228	        refine hp ⟨htop, fun {u v} huv => ?_⟩
   229	        by_cases hu : u ∈ I
   230	        · exact Or.inl hu
   231	        by_cases hv : v ∈ I
   232	        · exact Or.inr hv
   233	        exact absurd ⟨u, v, huv, hu, hv⟩ hcon
   234	      -- `J₁ = I ⊔ (a) > I`
   235	      have hJ₁gt : I < I ⊔ Ideal.span {a} :=
   236	        lt_of_le_of_ne le_sup_left (fun h => ha (by
   237	          rw [h]
   238	          exact Submodule.mem_sup_right (Ideal.mem_span_singleton_self a)))
   239	      -- `J₂ = (I : a) > I`
   240	      have hJ₂le : I ≤ Submodule.colon I {a} := fun r hr =>
   241	        Submodule.mem_colon_singleton.mpr
   242	          (by rw [smul_eq_mul]; exact Ideal.mul_mem_right a I hr)
   243	      have hJ₂gt : I < Submodule.colon I {a} :=
   244	        lt_of_le_of_ne hJ₂le (fun h => hb (by
   245	          rw [h]
   246	          exact Submodule.mem_colon_singleton.mpr
   247	            (by rw [smul_eq_mul, mul_comm]; exact hab)))
   248	      -- split `x = y + a•z` with `y ∈ I•⊤` through `P (I ⊔ (a))`
   249	      have hx₁ : x ∈ (I ⊔ Ideal.span {a}) • (⊤ : Submodule R M) :=
   250	        IH _ hJ₁gt x (Submodule.smul_mono_left le_sup_left hx)
   251	      rw [Submodule.sup_smul, Submodule.ideal_span_singleton_smul] at hx₁
   252	      obtain ⟨y, hy, z', hz', rfl⟩ := Submodule.mem_sup.mp hx₁
   253	      obtain ⟨z, -, rfl⟩ := (Submodule.mem_smul_pointwise_iff_exists z' a
   254	        (⊤ : Submodule R M)).mp hz'
   255	      -- `φ y ∈ I•⊤`, hence `a • φ z ∈ I•⊤`
   256	      have hφy : φ y ∈ I • (⊤ : Submodule R M) := by
   257	        have hmap := Submodule.map_smul'' I (⊤ : Submodule R M) φ
   258	        have : φ y ∈ Submodule.map φ (I • (⊤ : Submodule R M)) :=
   259	          Submodule.mem_map_of_mem hy
   260	        rw [hmap] at this
   261	        exact smul_mono_right I
   262	          (le_top : Submodule.map φ (⊤ : Submodule R M) ≤ ⊤) this
   263	      have haz : a • φ z ∈ I • (⊤ : Submodule R M) := by
   264	        have hsum : φ y + a • φ z ∈ I • (⊤ : Submodule R M) := by
   265	          have : φ (y + a • z) = φ y + a • φ z := by rw [map_add, map_smul]
   266	          rwa [this] at hx
   267	        simpa using Submodule.sub_mem _ hsum hφy
   268	      -- the flat colon lemma + `P ((I : a))`
   269	      have hz₂ : z ∈ Submodule.colon I {a} • (⊤ : Submodule R M) :=
   270	        IH _ hJ₂gt z
   271	          (Module.Flat.mem_colon_smul_top_of_smul_mem_smul_top I a haz)
   272	      -- `a • ((I : a)•⊤) ≤ I•⊤`
   273	      have haz₂ : a • z ∈ I • (⊤ : Submodule R M) := by
   274	        have hsub : ∀ w ∈ Submodule.colon I {a} • (⊤ : Submodule R M),
   275	            a • w ∈ I • (⊤ : Submodule R M) := by
   276	          intro w hw
   277	          refine Submodule.smul_induction_on hw (fun r hr m _ => ?_)
   278	            (fun u v hu hv => ?_)
   279	          · have hra : r * a ∈ I := by
   280	              have := Submodule.mem_colon_singleton.mp hr
   281	              rwa [smul_eq_mul] at this
   282	            rw [smul_smul, mul_comm a r]
   283	            exact Submodule.smul_mem_smul hra Submodule.mem_top
   284	          · rw [smul_add]
   285	            exact Submodule.add_mem _ hu hv
   286	        exact hsub z hz₂
   287	      exact Submodule.add_mem _ hy haz₂
   288	  intro u v huv
   289	  have hsub : φ (u - v) = 0 := by rw [map_sub, huv, sub_self]
   290	  have hmem : u - v ∈ (⊥ : Ideal R) • (⊤ : Submodule R M) :=
   291	    key ⊥ (u - v) (by rw [hsub, Submodule.bot_smul]; exact Submodule.zero_mem _)
   292	  rw [Submodule.bot_smul, Submodule.mem_bot] at hmem
   293	  exact sub_eq_zero.mp hmem
   294	
   295	end Core

   299	variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R] {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra R A]
   300	
   301	/-- The right-tensor of multiplication-by-`s` is multiplication by `s ⊗ 1` on the
   302	tensor-product algebra. -/
   303	theorem rTensor_mulLeft_eq_mulLeft_tmul (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
   304	    (s : A) :
   305	    (LinearMap.mulLeft R s).rTensor S =
   306	      LinearMap.mulLeft R (s ⊗ₜ[R] (1 : S) : A ⊗[R] S) := by
   307	  refine TensorProduct.ext' (fun a c => ?_)
   308	  rw [LinearMap.rTensor_tmul, LinearMap.mulLeft_apply, LinearMap.mulLeft_apply,
   309	    Algebra.TensorProduct.tmul_mul_tmul, one_mul]
   310	
   311	/-- **The `lm:ctn`-lite slicing criterion, ring form** (fibrewise-regular + flat ⟹
   312	regular; DAT-A2 core, DD-R's bridge): over a Noetherian ring `R`, an element of a flat
   313	`R`-algebra whose image `s ⊗ 1` is a nonzerodivisor in every residue-field fibre
   314	`A ⊗[R] κ(p)` is a nonzerodivisor. -/
   315	theorem Module.Flat.mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_forall_tmul_residueField
   316	    [IsNoetherianRing R] [Module.Flat R A] {s : A}
   317	    (hfib : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum R,
   318	      (s ⊗ₜ[R] (1 : p.asIdeal.ResidueField) : A ⊗[R] p.asIdeal.ResidueField) ∈
   319	        nonZeroDivisors (A ⊗[R] p.asIdeal.ResidueField)) :
   320	    s ∈ nonZeroDivisors A := by
   321	  have hinj : Function.Injective (LinearMap.mulLeft R s) := by
   322	    refine Module.Flat.injective_of_forall_rTensor_residueField_injective
   323	      (LinearMap.mulLeft R s) (fun p => ?_)
   324	    rw [rTensor_mulLeft_eq_mulLeft_tmul p.asIdeal.ResidueField s]
   325	    intro u v huv
   326	    have hzero : (u - v) * (s ⊗ₜ[R] (1 : p.asIdeal.ResidueField)) = 0 := by
   327	      rw [LinearMap.mulLeft_apply, LinearMap.mulLeft_apply] at huv
   328	      rw [sub_mul, mul_comm u, mul_comm v, huv, sub_self]
   329	    exact sub_eq_zero.mp ((mem_nonZeroDivisors_iff.mp (hfib p)).2 (u - v) hzero)
   330	  rw [mem_nonZeroDivisors_iff]
   331	  constructor
   332	  · intro z hz
   333	    have hmul : LinearMap.mulLeft R s z = LinearMap.mulLeft R s 0 := by
   334	      rw [LinearMap.mulLeft_apply, LinearMap.mulLeft_apply, mul_zero]
   335	      exact hz
   336	    exact hinj hmul
   337	  · intro z hz
   338	    have hmul : LinearMap.mulLeft R s z = LinearMap.mulLeft R s 0 := by
   339	      rw [LinearMap.mulLeft_apply, LinearMap.mulLeft_apply, mul_zero, mul_comm]
   340	      exact hz
   341	    exact hinj hmul
   342	
   343	end RingForm

     8	/-!
     9	# The section rank at a chart-locus point
    10	
    11	`Pic0ChartLocusH0One` specializes the chart parameter to the genus and obtains the
    12	unique-effective-representative value `h⁰ = 1`.  This file records the unspecialized
    13	calculation.  If the chart parameter is `n` and the curve has Euler characteristic
    14	`1 - g`, the vanishing witness extracted from `chartLocus` has
    15	
    16	`h⁰ = n + 1 - g`.
    17	
    18	This separates two roles that a coverage argument must not conflate: a large parameter can
    19	force `H¹`-vanishing, while the injective Abel chart needs the genus parameter, where the
    20	same rank formula becomes `h⁰ = 1`.
    21	-/

    45	/-- Chart-locus membership at parameter `n` supplies a witness of section rank `n + 1 - g` on a
    46	curve with Euler characteristic `1 - g`.
    47	
    48	The conclusion retains the presentation, divisor-class, degree, and vanishing clauses from
    49	`IsSplitWitness`; consequently it is tied to the given class and cannot be inhabited by an
    50	unrelated trivial divisor. -/
    51	theorem exists_splitting_h0_formula_of_mem_chartLocus
    52	    {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} (lam : picEt C T) (t : T.left)
    53	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor) (n g : ℕ)
    54	    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
    55	      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (n : ℤ))
    56	    (hχ : Sheaf.chi (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) = 1 - (g : ℤ))
    57	    (hlam : degAt lam (Over.testPoint t) = 0)
    58	    (ht : t ∈ chartLocus C m Z lam) :
    59	    ∃ (L : Type u) (_ : Field L) (_ : Algebra k L) (_ : Algebra (Over.testPointField t) L)
    60	        (_ : IsScalarTower k (Over.testPointField t) L)
    61	        (_ : Module.Finite (Over.testPointField t) L)
    62	        (_ : Algebra.IsSeparable (Over.testPointField t) L)
    63	        (M : (relCurve C L).CechPic)
    64	        (W : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).CurveDivisor),
    65	      PicEtAff.map C L
    66	          (picEtAffineEquiv C (Over.testPointField t)
    67	            (picEtMap C (Over.testPoint t) (chartTwist C m Z T lam)))
    68	        = PicEtAff.unit C L (relPicMk C (overSpec k L) M) ∧
    69	      Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L W = M ∧
    70	      Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg L W = (n : ℤ) ∧
    71	      Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule
    72	        ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.divisorSheaf L W) 1) ∧
    73	      (Sheaf.h0 ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.divisorSheaf L W) : ℤ)
    74	        = (n : ℤ) + 1 - (g : ℤ) := by
    75	  obtain ⟨L, hLf, hLa, hLKa, hLtow, hLfin, hLsep, M, hM, W, hWcl, hWh1⟩ := ht
    76	  haveI : IsIntegral (relCurve C L) := instIsIntegralBaseChange C L
    77	  haveI : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (relCurve C L ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of L)) :=
    78	    instSmoothOfRelativeDimensionBaseChange C L
    79	  haveI : QuasiCompact (relCurve C L ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of L)) :=
    80	    instQuasiCompactBaseChange C L
    81	  haveI : Module.Finite L (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C L).moduleKSheaf L) 0) :=
    82	    instModuleFiniteHModuleZeroBaseChange C L
    83	  haveI : Module.Finite L (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C L).moduleKSheaf L) 1) :=
    84	    instModuleFiniteHModuleOneBaseChange C L
    85	  have hWdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg L W = (n : ℤ) := by
    86	    rw [← classDeg_picClass (K := L) W, hWcl,
    87	      classDeg_presenting_eq_degAff C L _ M hM]
    88	    change degAt (chartTwist C m Z T lam) (Over.testPoint t) = (n : ℤ)
    89	    rw [chartTwist, degAt_mul, degAt_inv, degAt_mul, degAt_thetaFamily_pow,
    90	      degAt_sigmaFamily, hlam, hdeg]
    91	    ring
    92	  have hχL : Sheaf.chi (((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).moduleKSheaf L) = 1 - (g : ℤ) :=
    93	    chi_relCurve_baseField C L g hχ
    94	  have hrank := h0_eq_deg_add_chi_of_subsingleton_hModule_one (K := L) W hWh1
    95	  rw [hWdeg, hχL] at hrank
    96	  refine ⟨L, hLf, hLa, hLKa, hLtow, hLfin, hLsep, M, W, hM, hWcl, hWdeg, hWh1, ?_⟩
    97	  omega
    98	
    99	/-- Above the genus parameter, chart-locus membership supplies a witness with at least two
   100	sections.  Thus the
   101	large-parameter vanishing route and the `h⁰ = 1` uniqueness route are genuinely different
   102	branches of the representability argument. -/
   103	theorem exists_splitting_two_le_h0_of_mem_chartLocus
   104	    {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} (lam : picEt C T) (t : T.left)
   105	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor) (n g : ℕ)
   106	    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
   107	      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (n : ℤ))
   108	    (hχ : Sheaf.chi (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) = 1 - (g : ℤ))
   109	    (hlam : degAt lam (Over.testPoint t) = 0) (hgn : g < n)
   110	    (ht : t ∈ chartLocus C m Z lam) :
   111	    ∃ (L : Type u) (_ : Field L) (_ : Algebra k L) (_ : Algebra (Over.testPointField t) L)
   112	        (_ : IsScalarTower k (Over.testPointField t) L)
   113	        (_ : Module.Finite (Over.testPointField t) L)
   114	        (_ : Algebra.IsSeparable (Over.testPointField t) L)
   115	        (M : (relCurve C L).CechPic)
   116	        (W : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).CurveDivisor),
   117	      PicEtAff.map C L
   118	          (picEtAffineEquiv C (Over.testPointField t)
   119	            (picEtMap C (Over.testPoint t) (chartTwist C m Z T lam)))
   120	        = PicEtAff.unit C L (relPicMk C (overSpec k L) M) ∧
   121	      Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L W = M ∧
   122	      Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg L W = (n : ℤ) ∧
   123	      Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule
   124	        ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.divisorSheaf L W) 1) ∧
   125	      2 ≤ Sheaf.h0 ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.divisorSheaf L W) := by
   126	  obtain ⟨L, hLf, hLa, hLKa, hLtow, hLfin, hLsep, M, W, hM, hWcl, hWdeg, hWh1,
   127	      hrank⟩ := exists_splitting_h0_formula_of_mem_chartLocus
   128	        lam t m Z n g hdeg hχ hlam ht
   129	  refine ⟨L, hLf, hLa, hLKa, hLtow, hLfin, hLsep, M, W, hM, hWcl, hWdeg, hWh1, ?_⟩
   130	  have htwo : (2 : ℤ) ≤
   131	      (Sheaf.h0 ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.divisorSheaf L W) : ℤ) := by
   132	    rw [hrank]
   133	    omega
   134	  exact_mod_cast htwo

   136	/-! ## The actual unconditional coverage parameter -/
   137	
   138	/-- On a positive-genus curve, the unconditional admissible coverage parameter is strictly
   139	larger than the genus.
   140	
   141	The strictness does not add a cohomological hypothesis: `h⁰(𝒪_C) = 1` follows from the standing
   142	proper, smooth, geometrically irreducible assumptions.  If the ledger contribution above `g`
   143	were nonpositive, `genus_eq_zero_of_windowBound_nonpos` would contradict `g ≠ 0`. -/
   144	theorem genus_lt_admissibleCoverageParameter_of_ne_zero
   145	    {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite π] [IsDominant π]
   146	    (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom)
   147	    (g : ℕ) (hg : g ≠ 0)
   148	    (hχ : Sheaf.chi (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) = 1 - (g : ℤ)) :
   149	    letI : C.left.Over (Spec (.of k)) := ⟨C.hom⟩
   150	    haveI : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (C.left ↘ Spec (.of k)) :=
   151	      inferInstanceAs (SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom)
   152	    haveI : IsIntegral C.left := isIntegral_left_of_geometricallyReduced C
   153	    haveI : LocallyOfFiniteType (C.left ↘ Spec (.of k)) :=
   154	      inferInstanceAs (LocallyOfFiniteType C.hom)
   155	    haveI : QuasiCompact (C.left ↘ Spec (.of k)) :=
   156	      inferInstanceAs (QuasiCompact C.hom)
   157	    haveI : Module.Finite k (Sheaf.HModule (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) 0) :=
   158	      moduleFinite_hModule_zero C
   159	    haveI : Module.Finite k (Sheaf.HModule (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) 1) :=
   160	      moduleFinite_hModule_one C
   161	    g < admissibleCoverageParameter (C := C) hπ g := by
   162	  letI : C.left.Over (Spec (.of k)) := ⟨C.hom⟩
   163	  haveI : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (C.left ↘ Spec (.of k)) :=
   164	    inferInstanceAs (SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom)
   165	  haveI : IsIntegral C.left := isIntegral_left_of_geometricallyReduced C
   166	  haveI : LocallyOfFiniteType (C.left ↘ Spec (.of k)) :=
   167	    inferInstanceAs (LocallyOfFiniteType C.hom)
   168	  haveI : QuasiCompact (C.left ↘ Spec (.of k)) :=
   169	    inferInstanceAs (QuasiCompact C.hom)
   170	  haveI : Module.Finite k (Sheaf.HModule (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) 0) :=

    17	`Pic0ChartIndexLedgerFeed`.  Counting *any* spelling of the shape (so including the per-index
    18	`(nn i : ℤ)` form) gives 26, and 65 files bind a hypothesis *named* `hdeg` in some form; the
    19	figure that matters for this file is the first, since it is the exact binder the theorems below
    20	are about.  The hypothesis:
    21	
    22	  `hdeg : deg_k Z = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (n : ℤ)`
    23	
    24	with `m : ℕ` the twist exponent, `Z` the chart index and `n` the chart parameter.  **No file
    25	produces one.**  Every declaration mentioning it takes it as an argument, and the two theorems
    26	that conclude an `∃` over `(m, Z)` — `exists_chartIndex_mem_chartLocus_of_ledgerIndex`
    27	(`Pic0ChartCoverageThreshold.lean:349`) and `Pic0ChartCoverageNoDrop.lean:265` — take the same
    28	constraint as a hypothesis and say so in their docstrings.  So the whole chart layer is
    29	quantified over a datum whose inhabitation nothing had measured.
    30	
    31	This file measures it, and the answer is an equivalence with no geometry in it.
    32	
    33	## What is proved
    34	
    35	`chartIndex_iff_isDegree`: for any target `c : ℤ`,
    36	
    37	  `(∃ m Z, deg_k Z = m·d₁ − c)  ↔  (∃ W, deg_k W = c)`
    38	
    39	so the binder carries **exactly** the information that `c` lies in the image of
    40	`deg_k : CurveDivisor → ℤ`, and nothing else.
    41	
    42	Two consequences worth stating separately, because both correct a live pricing:
    43	
    44	* **The θ-exponent `m` is idle.**  The backward direction takes `m = 0` and `Z = −W`
    45	  (`chartIndex_of_isDegree`).  Every consumer's `m` is therefore free to be chosen for
    46	  *other* reasons; `hdeg` places no constraint on it, and a lane that reads the binder as
    47	  coupling `m` to `n` (the shape `Pic0ChartCoverageIndexSlack`'s `ledger_forces_b_eq_n`
    48	  suggests) is reading a coupling that the *chart parameter* creates, not this hypothesis.
    49	* **Admissibility is shift-invariant and subgroup-closed** (`isDegree_add_mul_iff`,
    50	  `isDegree_sub`): the admissible targets are an additive subgroup of `ℤ` containing every
    51	  multiple of `d₁`.  So admissibility at `n` and at `n + a·d₁` are the same statement — which
    52	  is what bears on parameter matching (`I-1345`): moving a chart parameter by a multiple of the
    53	  θ-degree is free on the `hdeg` side.
    54	
    55	## What this does NOT do, stated plainly
    56	
    57	It does **not** exhibit an admissible `n` other than the multiples of `d₁`.  The equivalence is
    58	a reduction, not an inhabitation: over an arbitrary base field `deg_k` is weighted by residue
    59	degrees (`RiemannRoch/Divisor.lean:61`), so its image is a proper subgroup `index·ℤ` in general,
    60	and the tree's only route to a residue-degree-one point needs `[IsSepClosed k]`
    61	(`Curve/SepPointsDense.lean:278`), which `archon-protected.yaml`'s arbitrary-field statement
    62	forbids assuming.  **So `hdeg` at `n = g` is NOT known to be satisfiable**, and this file does
    63	not claim it is.  What it establishes is that the question is arithmetic — the image of one
    64	group homomorphism — rather than anything about charts, certificates or representability.
    65	
    66	Nor does it discharge any antecedent of `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts`: `IsChartUniv`, coverage
    67	and `rep` are untouched.  What it removes is an obligation nobody had noticed was there, and it
    68	tells three other rows which parameter moves are free.
    69	
    70	## Main declarations
    71	
    72	* `AlgebraicGeometry.IsDivisorDegree` — the predicate "`c` is the degree of some divisor".
    73	* `AlgebraicGeometry.chartIndex_of_isDegree` — the producer, with `m = 0`.
    74	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isDegree_of_chartIndex` — the converse, so nothing is weakened.
    75	* `AlgebraicGeometry.chartIndex_iff_isDegree` — the equivalence.
    76	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isDegree_mul_thetaDeg` — every multiple of `d₁` is admissible.
    77	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isDegree_add_mul_iff` — shift-invariance by multiples of `d₁`.
    78	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isDegree_mul_thetaDeg_add_iff` — the same, with the multiple written first,
    79	  which is the shape the ledger consumer's target `M·δ + g` has.
    80	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isDegree_sub` — subgroup closure.
    81	-/

    99	/-! ## The predicate -/
   100	
   101	variable (C) in
   102	/-- **`c` is a divisor degree on the base-changed curve `C_k = (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left`.**
   103	
   104	Named rather than inlined so that the three shift/closure facts below are about one object and
   105	are findable by a name search, and so that consumers of `hdeg` can cite the reduction rather
   106	than re-deriving it (the `I-1341` lesson: an inlined `have` is invisible to every search). -/
   107	def IsDivisorDegree (c : ℤ) : Prop :=
   108	  ∃ W : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor, Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k W = c
   109	
   110	/-! ## The equivalence -/
   111	
   112	variable (C) in
   113	/-- **The producer: `hdeg` at parameter `c` from a divisor of degree `c`, with `m = 0`.**
   114	
   115	The witness is `⟨0, -W⟩`.  This is the direction that matters for the 23 consumers, and the
   116	fact that `m = 0` works is the measurement that the θ-exponent is *not* coupled to the chart
   117	parameter by this hypothesis. -/
   118	theorem chartIndex_of_isDegree {c : ℤ} (h : IsDivisorDegree C c) :
   119	    ∃ (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor),
   120	      Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - c := by
   121	  obtain ⟨W, hW⟩ := h
   122	  refine ⟨0, -W, ?_⟩
   123	  rw [Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg_neg, hW]
   124	  ring
   125	
   126	variable (C) in
   127	/-- **The converse**, so this file claims no reduction it has not earned (the `I-0896`
   128	criterion): from any legal chart index at parameter `c`, the parameter *is* a divisor degree.
   129	
   130	The witness is `m • F − Z` for `F` the fibre Weil divisor of `thetaP1 C`, whose degree is
   131	`d₁ = classDeg k (thetaCechClass C)` by `classDeg_fiberTwist_one`. -/
   132	theorem isDegree_of_chartIndex {c : ℤ} (m : ℕ)
   133	    (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
   134	    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
   135	      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - c) :
   136	    IsDivisorDegree C c := by
   137	  haveI := isFinite_thetaP1 (C := C)
   138	  haveI := isDominant_thetaP1 (C := C)
   139	  refine ⟨m • fiberWeilDivisor (thetaP1 C) - Z, ?_⟩
   140	  rw [Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg_sub' k, Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg_nsmul' k, hdeg,
   141	    ← classDeg_fiberTwist_one (thetaP1 C)]
   142	  change (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C)
   143	    - ((m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - c) = c
   144	  ring

   146	variable (C) in
   147	/-- **THE MEASUREMENT**: the chart-index binder carries exactly "`c` is a divisor degree".
   148	
   149	Both directions are one rewrite each.  The content is not the proof — it is that the question
   150	"is the chart layer's `hdeg` inhabitable, and at which parameters?" is the question "what is the
   151	image of `deg_k`?", with no chart, certificate or representation in it. -/
   152	theorem chartIndex_iff_isDegree (c : ℤ) :
   153	    (∃ (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor),
   154	      Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - c)

   156	  ⟨fun ⟨m, Z, hZ⟩ => isDegree_of_chartIndex C m Z hZ, chartIndex_of_isDegree C⟩
   157	
   158	/-! ## What IS inhabited, and how admissibility moves -/
   159	
   160	variable (C) in
   161	/-- **Every multiple of the θ-degree is admissible** — `a` copies of the fibre divisor.
   162	
   163	This is the only inhabitation this file offers, and it is honest about being weak: it says the
   164	chart layer can be run at `n` a multiple of `d₁`, and says nothing about `n = g`. -/
   165	theorem isDegree_mul_thetaDeg (a : ℕ) :
   166	    IsDivisorDegree C ((a : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C)) := by
   167	  haveI := isFinite_thetaP1 (C := C)
   168	  haveI := isDominant_thetaP1 (C := C)
   169	  refine ⟨a • fiberWeilDivisor (thetaP1 C), ?_⟩
   170	  rw [Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg_nsmul' k, ← classDeg_fiberTwist_one (thetaP1 C)]
   171	  rfl
   172	
   173	variable (C) in
   174	/-- **Shift-invariance by multiples of `d₁`**, in both directions.
   175	
   176	This is the fact that bears on parameter matching (`I-1345`, and `Pic0ChartAtlasParamFree`'s
   177	question "at which parameters is `divFunctor C π n` representable?"): on the `hdeg` side,
   178	moving a chart parameter by a multiple of the θ-degree costs nothing.  It does **not** say the
   179	`rep` side moves — that is the open half. -/
   180	theorem isDegree_add_mul_iff (c : ℤ) (a : ℕ) :
   181	    IsDivisorDegree C c
   182	      ↔ IsDivisorDegree C (c + (a : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C)) := by
   183	  haveI := isFinite_thetaP1 (C := C)
   184	  haveI := isDominant_thetaP1 (C := C)
   185	  have hF : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k (a • fiberWeilDivisor (thetaP1 C))
   186	      = (a : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) := by
   187	    rw [Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg_nsmul' k, ← classDeg_fiberTwist_one (thetaP1 C)]
   188	    rfl
   189	  constructor
   190	  · rintro ⟨W, hW⟩
   191	    exact ⟨W + a • fiberWeilDivisor (thetaP1 C), by
   192	      rw [Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg_add, hW, hF]⟩
   193	  · rintro ⟨W, hW⟩
   194	    refine ⟨W - a • fiberWeilDivisor (thetaP1 C), ?_⟩
   195	    rw [Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg_sub' k, hW, hF]
   196	    ring
   197	
   198	omit [IsProper C.hom] in
   199	variable (C) in
   200	/-- **The admissible targets are closed under subtraction** — hence an additive subgroup of
   201	`ℤ`, since `0` is admissible by `W = 0`.
   202	
   203	Recorded because it is what makes "the image of `deg_k` is `index·ℤ`" a *theorem shape* rather
   204	than a docstring remark: three files assert the `index·ℤ` form in prose
   205	(`JacobianDataAbelDegreeWindow.lean:23`, `:200`, `JacobianDataAbelEffective.lean:128`) and none

   207	theorem isDegree_sub {c c' : ℤ} (h : IsDivisorDegree C c) (h' : IsDivisorDegree C c') :
   208	    IsDivisorDegree C (c - c') := by
   209	  obtain ⟨W, hW⟩ := h
   210	  obtain ⟨W', hW'⟩ := h'
   211	  exact ⟨W - W', by rw [Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg_sub' k, hW, hW']⟩
   212	
   213	omit [IsProper C.hom] in
   214	variable (C) in
   215	/-- `0` is admissible, by the zero divisor — the subgroup's unit. -/
   216	theorem isDegree_zero : IsDivisorDegree C 0 :=
   217	  ⟨0, by simp⟩
   218	
   219	variable (C) in
   220	/-- **A target of the shape `a·d₁ + c` is admissible exactly when `c` is** — the form the
   221	ledger consumer meets, with the summands in the order the ledger writes them.
   222	
   223	`isDegree_add_mul_iff` with the sum commuted.  Recorded separately because the coverage
   224	consumer's target is `M·δ + g`, i.e. the multiple **first**, and a consumer should not have to
   225	insert a `ring` step to use the shift.  This is the fact that turns the residue of
   226	`Pic0ChartIndexLedgerFeed`'s ledger theorem into a question about the **genus** rather than
   227	about the ledger constants — *provided* `M·δ` is a multiple of `d₁`, which is a separate
   228	hypothesis about `π` versus `thetaP1 C` and is **not** proved anywhere.
   229	
   230	What *is* free, measured by `rfl` and recorded so nobody prices it: `windowδ (thetaP1 C)` and
   231	`classDeg k (thetaCechClass C)` are the same term, both unfolding to
   232	`classDeg k (fiberTwist (thetaP1 C) 1)`.  So no `windowδ`-versus-`classDeg` plumbing is owed.
   233	
   234	A first draft added "so the open gap is two maps to `ℙ¹` on **two different curves**", and that
   235	was **false** — the two curves differ by base change along `k → k`, which is an isomorphism, and
   236	`Pic0ChartIndexLedgerFeed.isDivisorDegree_iff_left` transports this whole predicate to `C.left`
   237	from declarations that were already in scope.  Withdrawn.  The open gap is the two **maps** on
   238	**one** curve: is `deg (fibre of π)` commensurable with `deg (fibre of thetaP1 C)`? -/
   239	theorem isDegree_mul_thetaDeg_add_iff (a : ℕ) (c : ℤ) :
   240	    IsDivisorDegree C ((a : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) + c)
   241	      ↔ IsDivisorDegree C c := by
   242	  have hcomm : c + (a : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C)
   243	      = (a : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) + c := by ring
   244	  refine ⟨fun h => (isDegree_add_mul_iff C c a).mpr (by rwa [hcomm]), fun h => ?_⟩
   245	  have := (isDegree_add_mul_iff C c a).mp h
   246	  rwa [hcomm] at this

    12	/-!
    13	# Local generators of a finite projective module (DAT-A generators corollary)
    14	
    15	Worksheet §2.2.3a (`informal/spec-dat-a.md` §4): for a finite projective module `Q`
    16	over `B` — the engine's `H⁰` on the fibrewise-vanishing locus (`datumRigidEngine`) —
    17	and a prime `p` where the fibre `Q ⊗ κ(p)` is nontrivial, there is a basic open
    18	`D(f) ∋ p` and a GLOBAL element `q : Q` whose image in `Q ⊗ κ(q')` is nonzero for
    19	EVERY `q' ∈ D(f)`:
    20	
    21	> Zariski-locally on `Spec B`, a fibrewise-nonzero section exists.
    22	
    23	Route: finite + projective ⟹ finitely presented + flat; `Module.freeLocus_eq_univ`
    24	gives freeness at `p`; `Module.FinitePresentation.exists_free_localizedModule_powers`
    25	localizes the freeness to a basic open `D(f)`; a basis element of the localized module
    26	has numerator `q`; at every `q' ∈ D(f)` the coordinate functional of the basis,
    27	composed with the away-lift `B_f →+* κ(q')` (legal since `f ∉ q'` makes `f` invertible
    28	in the residue field), evaluates the fibre image of `q` to a nonzero power of the image
    29	of `f` — no localized tensor products are formed.
    30	
    31	Consumers (stated for verbatim consumption): DAT-B's coverage (a local divisor
    32	presentation of an arbitrary functor point through DAT-A's `sectionLocalEquations`) and
    33	DD-R's local generators (dat-d-worksheet §3.4). The `Nontrivial` fibre input is the
    34	rank clause consumers hold through FLV/DAT-3.
    35	-/

    37	set_option autoImplicit false

    39	universe u
    40	
    41	open scoped TensorProduct
    42	
    43	namespace Module
    44	
    45	variable {B : Type u} [CommRing B] {Q : Type u} [AddCommGroup Q] [Module B Q]
    46	
    47	/-- If some localization of `Q` away from an element of `p.primeCompl` is trivial, the
    48	residue-field fibre at `p` is trivial: the annihilating power of `f` is invertible in
    49	`κ(p)`. -/
    50	private lemma subsingleton_tensor_residueField_of_subsingleton_away
    51	    (p : PrimeSpectrum B) (f : B) (hf : f ∉ p.asIdeal)
    52	    (hsub : Subsingleton (LocalizedModule.Away f Q)) :
    53	    Subsingleton (Q ⊗[B] p.asIdeal.ResidueField) := by
    54	  have hx : algebraMap B p.asIdeal.ResidueField f ≠ 0 := fun h0 =>
    55	    hf (Ideal.algebraMap_residueField_eq_zero.mp h0)
    56	  refine subsingleton_of_forall_eq 0 (fun z => ?_)
    57	  induction z using TensorProduct.induction_on with
    58	  | zero => rfl
    59	  | add u v hu hv => rw [hu, hv, add_zero]
    60	  | tmul q c =>
    61	      -- the localized image of `q` vanishes, so a power of `f` kills `q`
    62	      have hmk : (LocalizedModule.mk q 1 : LocalizedModule.Away f Q)
    63	          = LocalizedModule.mk 0 1 := Subsingleton.elim _ _
    64	      obtain ⟨u, hu⟩ := LocalizedModule.mk_eq.mp hmk
    65	      rw [one_smul, one_smul, smul_zero] at hu
    66	      -- transfer `u • q = 0` through the tensor, inverting `u` in the residue field
    67	      have hu_ne : algebraMap B p.asIdeal.ResidueField (u : B) ≠ 0 := by
    68	        obtain ⟨n, hn⟩ := u.2
    69	        intro h0
    70	        rw [← hn, map_pow] at h0
    71	        exact hx (pow_eq_zero_iff' .. |>.mp h0).1
    72	      have hu' : (u : B) • q = 0 := hu
    73	      have hkill : q ⊗ₜ[B] ((algebraMap B p.asIdeal.ResidueField (u : B))
    74	          * ((algebraMap B p.asIdeal.ResidueField (u : B))⁻¹ * c)) = 0 := by
    75	        have hz : ((u : B) • q) ⊗ₜ[B]
    76	            ((algebraMap B p.asIdeal.ResidueField (u : B))⁻¹ * c) = 0 := by
    77	          rw [hu', TensorProduct.zero_tmul]
    78	        rw [TensorProduct.smul_tmul, Algebra.smul_def] at hz
    79	        exact hz
    80	      rwa [mul_inv_cancel_left₀ hu_ne] at hkill
    81	
    82	/-- **The generators corollary** (worksheet §2.2.3a; DAT-B/DD-R's local generators):
    83	for a finite projective `B`-module `Q` with nontrivial residue-field fibre at `p`,
    84	there are `f ∉ p` and a global `q : Q` whose image in `Q ⊗ κ(q')` is nonzero for
    85	**every** prime `q'` of the basic open `D(f)` — Zariski-locally, a fibrewise-nonzero
    86	section of `Q` exists. -/
    87	theorem exists_fibrewise_tmul_ne_zero_of_projective
    88	    [Module.Finite B Q] [Module.Projective B Q] (p : PrimeSpectrum B)
    89	    (hp : Nontrivial (Q ⊗[B] p.asIdeal.ResidueField)) :
    90	    ∃ f : B, f ∉ p.asIdeal ∧ ∃ q : Q, ∀ q' : PrimeSpectrum B, f ∉ q'.asIdeal →
    91	      (q ⊗ₜ (1 : q'.asIdeal.ResidueField) : Q ⊗[B] q'.asIdeal.ResidueField) ≠ 0 := by
    92	  classical
    93	  haveI : Module.FinitePresentation B Q := Module.finitePresentation_of_projective B Q
    94	  -- freeness at `p`, localized to a basic open `D(f)`
    95	  haveI hfree_p : Module.Free (Localization.AtPrime p.asIdeal)
    96	      (LocalizedModule.AtPrime p.asIdeal Q) := by
    97	    have hmem : p ∈ Module.freeLocus B Q := by
    98	      rw [Module.freeLocus_eq_univ]
    99	      trivial
   100	    exact Module.mem_freeLocus.mp hmem
   101	  obtain ⟨f, hf, hfree, -⟩ :=
   102	    Module.FinitePresentation.exists_free_localizedModule_powers p.asIdeal.primeCompl
   103	      (LocalizedModule.mkLinearMap p.asIdeal.primeCompl Q)
   104	      (Localization.AtPrime p.asIdeal)
   105	  haveI := hfree
   106	  -- the localized module is nontrivial (else the fibre at `p` would be trivial)
   107	  haveI hnt : Nontrivial (LocalizedModule.Away f Q) := by
   108	    by_contra hns
   109	    rw [not_nontrivial_iff_subsingleton] at hns
   110	    exact (not_subsingleton _)
   111	      (subsingleton_tensor_residueField_of_subsingleton_away p f hf hns)
   112	  -- a basis element, with numerator `q` and denominator a power of `f`
   113	  let b := Module.Free.chooseBasis (Localization (.powers f)) (LocalizedModule.Away f Q)
   114	  obtain ⟨i₀⟩ := b.index_nonempty
   115	  obtain ⟨⟨q, s⟩, hqs⟩ : ∃ ms : Q × (Submonoid.powers f),
   116	      (LocalizedModule.mk ms.1 ms.2 : LocalizedModule.Away f Q) = b i₀ :=
   117	    LocalizedModule.induction_on (fun m s => ⟨(m, s), rfl⟩) (b i₀)
   118	  refine ⟨f, hf, q, fun q' hq' => ?_⟩
   119	  -- the residue field of `q'` receives the away-localization
   120	  have hx : algebraMap B q'.asIdeal.ResidueField f ≠ 0 := fun h0 =>
   121	    hq' (Ideal.algebraMap_residueField_eq_zero.mp h0)
   122	  have hxu : IsUnit (algebraMap B q'.asIdeal.ResidueField f) :=
   123	    isUnit_iff_ne_zero.mpr hx
   124	  set g' : Localization (Submonoid.powers f) →+* q'.asIdeal.ResidueField :=
   125	    IsLocalization.Away.lift f hxu with hg'
   126	  -- the evaluation functional: coordinate of the basis at `i₀`, pushed to `κ(q')`
   127	  set Λ : Q ⊗[B] q'.asIdeal.ResidueField →ₗ[B] q'.asIdeal.ResidueField :=
   128	    TensorProduct.lift (LinearMap.mk₂ B
   129	      (fun m c => g' ((b.coord i₀) (LocalizedModule.mk m 1)) * c)
   130	      (fun m m' c => by
   131	        rw [show (LocalizedModule.mk (m + m') 1 : LocalizedModule.Away f Q)
   132	            = LocalizedModule.mk m 1 + LocalizedModule.mk m' 1 from
   133	          (LocalizedModule.mkLinearMap (.powers f) Q).map_add m m', map_add, map_add,
   134	          add_mul])
   135	      (fun a m c => by

   117	      change e₀.symm (algebraMap K (Localization.Away (g i)) a) = a
   118	      rw [← e₀.commutes a]
   119	      exact e₀.symm_apply_apply _
   120	    calc (DivFam.mapAlgHom e.toAlgHom (DivFam.mk Gᵢ)).toZar
   121	        = DivFamZar.mapAlgHom e.toAlgHom (DivFam.mk Gᵢ).toZar :=
   122	          DivFam.toZar_mapAlgHom e.toAlgHom (DivFam.mk Gᵢ)
   123	      _ = DivFamZar.mapAlgHom e.toAlgHom
   124	            (DivFamZar.mapAlgHom (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom k K (Localization.Away (g i)))
   125	              (DivFamZar.mk dp.1 dp.2)) := by
   126	          rw [htoZar, DivFamZar.mapAlgHom_eq_mapAlg
   127	            (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom k K (Localization.Away (g i))) (fun _ => rfl)]
   128	      _ = DivFamZar.mapAlgHom (AlgHom.id k K) (DivFamZar.mk dp.1 dp.2) := by
   129	          rw [← DivFamZar.mapAlgHom_comp, hcomp]
   130	      _ = ⟦dp⟧ := DivFamZar.mapAlgHom_id _
   131	
   132	/-- **The field-level degree law of the Abel ledger** (worksheet §4.2, bottom rows):
   133	the Čech Picard class of a locally certified divisor class of degree `n` over a field
   134	has `classDeg = n` — E-i (`classDeg_picClass`) composed with the CRT degree identity
   135	(`deg_divFamDivisor`) on a globally certified representative. -/
   136	theorem DivFamZar.classDeg_picClass
   137	    [IsIntegral (relCurve C K)]
   138	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (relCurve C K ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
   139	    [QuasiCompact (relCurve C K ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
   140	    [Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C K).moduleKSheaf K) 0)]
   141	    [Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C K).moduleKSheaf K) 1)]
   142	    (F₀ : DivFamZar C K π n) :
   143	    classDeg K F₀.picClass = (n : ℤ) := by
   144	  obtain ⟨G, rfl⟩ := DivFam.exists_toZar_eq F₀
   145	  rw [DivFamZar.picClass_toZar]
   146	  induction G using Quotient.inductionOn with
   147	  | h F =>
   148	    calc classDeg K (DivFam.picClass (DivFam.mk F))
   149	        = classDeg K F.eqns.presentation.picClass := by
   150	          rw [DivFam.picClass_mk, Scheme.LocalEquations.presentation_picClass]
   151	      _ = classDeg K (Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass K
   152	            (Scheme.presentationDivisor K F.eqns.presentation)) := by
   153	          rw [Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass_presentationDivisor]
   154	      _ = Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg K (Scheme.presentationDivisor K F.eqns.presentation) :=
   155	          _root_.AlgebraicGeometry.classDeg_picClass K _
   156	      _ = (n : ℤ) := by
   157	          rw [show Scheme.presentationDivisor K F.eqns.presentation
   158	              = divFamDivisor (DivFam.mk F) from (divFamDivisor_mk F).symm]
   159	          exact deg_divFamDivisor (DivFam.mk F)
   160	
   161	end Field

   167	variable (C π) in
   168	/-- The Abel transformation at an affine test, plus-construction form: the étale-unit
   169	image of the relative Picard class of `𝒪(F₀)`. -/
   170	def abelDivPlus (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] (F₀ : DivFamZar C A π n) :
   171	    PicEtAff C A :=
   172	  PicEtAff.unit C A (relPicMk C (overSpec k A) F₀.picClass)
   173	
   174	variable (C π) in
   175	/-- **The Abel transformation at an affine test** (worksheet §4.1): the `picEt`-valued
   176	form, through the unit of the étale sheafification. -/
   177	def abelDivAff (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] (F₀ : DivFamZar C A π n) :
   178	    picEt C (overSpec k A) :=
   179	  relPicToPicEt C (overSpec k A) (relPicMk C (overSpec k A) F₀.picClass)
   180	
   181	/-- The affine collapse of the `picEt`-valued Abel value is the plus-construction
   182	form. -/
   183	theorem picEtAffineEquiv_abelDivAff (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
   184	    (F₀ : DivFamZar C A π n) :
   185	    picEtAffineEquiv C A (abelDivAff C π A F₀) = abelDivPlus C π A F₀ :=
   186	  picEtAffineEquiv_relPicToPicEt C A _
   187	
   188	/-- **Naturality of the affine Abel transformation in the test algebra** (worksheet
   189	§4.1: `picClass_mapAlg` + `PicEtAff.mapAlg_unit`): base change of the Abel value is
   190	the Abel value of the base-changed class. -/
   191	theorem abelDivPlus_mapAlgHom {A B : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] [CommRing B]
   192	    [Algebra k B] (φ : A →ₐ[k] B) (F₀ : DivFamZar C A π n) :
   193	    PicEtAff.mapAlg C φ (abelDivPlus C π A F₀)
   194	      = abelDivPlus C π B (DivFamZar.mapAlgHom φ F₀) := by
   195	  letI : Algebra A B := φ.toRingHom.toAlgebra
   196	  haveI : IsScalarTower k A B := .of_algebraMap_eq fun a => (φ.commutes a).symm
   197	  have hclass : (DivFamZar.mapAlgHom φ F₀).picClass
   198	      = Scheme.CechPic.map (C ◁ Over.overSpecMap φ).left F₀.picClass := by
   199	    have hcurve : relCurveMap C A B = (C ◁ Over.overSpecMap φ).left := by
   200	      refine congrArg (fun ψ : overSpec k B ⟶ overSpec k A => (C ◁ ψ).left) ?_
   201	      exact Over.OverMorphism.ext rfl
   202	    rw [← hcurve]
   203	    exact DivFamZar.picClass_mapAlg B n F₀
   204	  calc PicEtAff.mapAlg C φ (abelDivPlus C π A F₀)
   205	      = PicEtAff.unit C B (relPicAlgMap C φ
   206	          (relPicMk C (overSpec k A) F₀.picClass)) := PicEtAff.mapAlg_unit C φ _
   207	    _ = PicEtAff.unit C B (relPicMk C (overSpec k B)
   208	          (Scheme.CechPic.map (C ◁ Over.overSpecMap φ).left F₀.picClass)) :=
   209	        congrArg (PicEtAff.unit C B)
   210	          (relPicMap_mk C (Over.overSpecMap φ) F₀.picClass)
   211	    _ = abelDivPlus C π B (DivFamZar.mapAlgHom φ F₀) := by
   212	        rw [abelDivPlus, hclass]
   213	
   214	end AbelAff

   251	      (picEtAffineEquiv_abelDivAff A (divFamZarAffineEquiv C π n A s)).symm)

   257	Abel value along an arbitrary test morphism is the Abel value of the restricted

   268	    abelDivPlus_mapAlgHom (Over.appLEAlgHom f V.1 W₀.1 hV) (s.1 V),
   269	    divFamZar.mapVal_spec C π n f s W W₀ hW₀ V hV]

   273	/-- **The degree ledger** (worksheet §4.2): the Abel value of a degree-`n` family has
   274	degree `n` at every field point — naturality reduces to the affine collapse at the
   275	field, `degAff_unit` + `relPicDeg_relPicMk` read the class degree, and the field-level
   276	degree law finishes. -/
   277	theorem degAt_abelDiv {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} (s : divFamZar C π n T) {K : Type u}
   278	    [Field K] [Algebra k K] (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T) :
   279	    degAt (abelDiv C π n T s) t = (n : ℤ) := by
   280	  haveI : IsIntegral (relCurve C K) := instIsIntegralBaseChange C K
   281	  haveI : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (relCurve C K ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) :=
   282	    instSmoothOfRelativeDimensionBaseChange C K
   283	  haveI : QuasiCompact (relCurve C K ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) :=
   284	    instQuasiCompactBaseChange C K
   285	  haveI : Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C K).moduleKSheaf K) 0) :=
   286	    instModuleFiniteHModuleZeroBaseChange C K
   287	  haveI : Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C K).moduleKSheaf K) 1) :=
   288	    instModuleFiniteHModuleOneBaseChange C K

   290	      (picEtMap C t (abelDiv C π n T s))) = (n : ℤ)
   291	  rw [picEtMap_abelDiv, picEtAffineEquiv_abelDiv]
   292	  change PicEtAff.degAff K (PicEtAff.unit C K (relPicMk C (overSpec k K)
   293	      (divFamZarAffineEquiv C π n K (divFamZar.map C π n t s)).picClass)) = (n : ℤ)
   294	  rw [PicEtAff.degAff_unit, relPicDeg_relPicMk]
   295	  exact DivFamZar.classDeg_picClass _

   298	/-- **The Abel natural transformation into the degree-`n` layer** (the sharpened
   299	dat-d Addendum row, worksheet §4.2): the Abel transformation, ledgered by

   301	`divFunctor C π n ⟶ picDegLayerFunctor C n`. -/

    15	/-!
    16	# Fibrewise regularity — the `lm:ctn`-lite slicing lemmas (DAT-A2 core)
    17	
    18	**THE SHARED TOR-LEMMA HOME** for the Wave-4 DATUM campaign (`informal/spec-dat-a.md`
    19	§1; coordination rule of the DAT-A/DD-1 lanes): Kleiman `lm:ctn` (iii)⟹(i)
    20	(`references/kleiman-picard-src/kleiman-picard.tex` 1786–1815) in a Tor-free spelling —
    21	
    22	> over a Noetherian base `R`, an `R`-linear endomorphism of a **flat** module that is
    23	> injective on every residue-field fibre is injective;
    24	
    25	in particular an element of a flat `R`-algebra whose image in every residue-field fibre
    26	is a nonzerodivisor is a nonzerodivisor (`fibrewise-regular + flat ⟹ regular`).
    27	
    28	The paper's Tor/local-flatness-criterion computation is replaced by a **Noetherian
    29	induction on ideals** with the predicate `P I := ∀ x, φ x ∈ I•⊤ → x ∈ I•⊤`:
    30	
    31	* `I = ⊤` is trivial; at a **prime** `p` the fibre hypothesis applies directly, through
    32	  the injection `M ⧸ p•⊤ ↪ M ⊗ κ(p)` (flatness of `M` against
    33	  `R⧸p ↪ κ(p)`, `Module.Flat.mem_smul_top_of_tmul_residueField_one_eq_zero`) — no
    34	  inductive hypothesis is consumed;
    35	* at a **non-prime** `I ≠ ⊤`, pick `a·b ∈ I` with `a, b ∉ I`; then `I ⊔ (a)` and the
    36	  colon `(I : a)` are both strictly larger, and the **flat colon lemma**
    37	  (`Module.Flat.mem_colon_smul_top_of_smul_mem_smul_top`: for flat `M`,
    38	  `a•x ∈ I•⊤ ⟹ x ∈ (I : a)•⊤`) splices the two inductive hypotheses together.
    39	
    40	Both flat inputs are *injectivity of a composite* through
    41	`TensorProduct.tensorQuotEquivQuotSMul` — no `Function.Exact`, no Tor, no local
    42	criterion of flatness. Mathlib does not have the slicing criterion in any form
    43	(searched 2026-07-17; only the converse directions exist:
    44	`IsSMulRegular.of_isLocalization`, `IsWeaklyRegular.of_flat`).
    45	
    46	`[IsNoetherianRing R]` is route-consistent: the DAT-1 engine keystone
    47	(`datumRigidEngine`) already assumes it, and (V-rel-B) runs over the RE-5 Noetherian
    48	descent stage.
    49	
    50	## Seam (DD-1a) — do not duplicate elsewhere
    51	
    52	The *other* half of `lm:ctn` used by the DAT-D lane — (i)⟹ base-change stability of a
    53	regular element with **flat quotient** (`0 → B → B → B/(f) → 0` with `B/(f)` flat stays
    54	exact after `⊗_R R'`; tex 1747–1770, dat-d-worksheet §1.2 DD-1a) — belongs in THIS file
    55	when the DD-1 lane lands it.
    56	
    57	## Main declarations
    58	
    59	* `Module.Flat.mem_colon_smul_top_of_smul_mem_smul_top` — the flat colon lemma;
    60	* `Module.Flat.mem_smul_top_of_tmul_residueField_one_eq_zero` — the prime-fibre kernel
    61	  computation `ker (M → M ⊗ κ(p)) = p•⊤` (the ⊇ half is
    62	  `tmul_residueField_one_eq_zero_of_mem_smul_top`, no flatness);
    63	* `Module.Flat.injective_of_forall_rTensor_residueField_injective` — **the core**;
    64	* `Module.Flat.mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_forall_tmul_residueField` — the ring form

    74	section ColonLemma
    75	
    76	variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R] {M : Type v} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
    77	
    78	/-- The multiplication-by-`a` map `R ⧸ (I : a) →ₗ[R] R ⧸ I`. It is injective by the
    79	definition of the colon ideal (`mapQSMul_injective`). -/
    80	private noncomputable def mapQSMul (I : Ideal R) (a : R) :
    81	    (R ⧸ Submodule.colon I {a}) →ₗ[R] (R ⧸ I) :=
    82	  Submodule.mapQ (Submodule.colon I {a}) I (LinearMap.lsmul R R a)
    83	    (fun r hr => by
    84	      have : r • a ∈ I := Submodule.mem_colon_singleton.mp hr
    85	      simpa [LinearMap.lsmul_apply, smul_eq_mul, mul_comm] using this)
    86	
    87	private lemma mapQSMul_mk (I : Ideal R) (a : R) (r : R) :
    88	    mapQSMul I a (Submodule.Quotient.mk r) = Submodule.Quotient.mk (a * r) := by
    89	  rw [mapQSMul, Submodule.mapQ_apply, LinearMap.lsmul_apply, smul_eq_mul]
    90	
    91	private lemma mapQSMul_injective (I : Ideal R) (a : R) :
    92	    Function.Injective (mapQSMul I a) := by
    93	  rw [← LinearMap.ker_eq_bot, eq_bot_iff]
    94	  intro x hx
    95	  obtain ⟨r, rfl⟩ := Submodule.Quotient.mk_surjective _ x
    96	  rw [LinearMap.mem_ker, mapQSMul_mk, Submodule.Quotient.mk_eq_zero] at hx
    97	  rw [Submodule.mem_bot, Submodule.Quotient.mk_eq_zero, Submodule.mem_colon_singleton,
    98	    smul_eq_mul, mul_comm]
    99	  exact hx
   100	
   101	/-- **The flat colon lemma**: over a flat module, dividing a smul-membership
   102	`a • x ∈ I • ⊤` by `a` lands in the colon ideal: `x ∈ (I : a) • ⊤`. Injectivity of
   103	`R ⧸ (I : a) → R ⧸ I` is preserved by `− ⊗ M`, and under
   104	`TensorProduct.tensorQuotEquivQuotSMul` the tensored map reads
   105	`x mod (I : a)•⊤ ↦ a•x mod I•⊤`. -/
   106	theorem Module.Flat.mem_colon_smul_top_of_smul_mem_smul_top [Module.Flat R M]
   107	    (I : Ideal R) (a : R) {x : M} (h : a • x ∈ I • (⊤ : Submodule R M)) :
   108	    x ∈ Submodule.colon I {a} • (⊤ : Submodule R M) := by
   109	  set J : Ideal R := Submodule.colon I {a} with hJ
   110	  -- chase `mk x` through `M ⧸ J•⊤ ≃ M ⊗ (R⧸J) → M ⊗ (R⧸I) ≃ M ⧸ I•⊤`
   111	  have h1 : (TensorProduct.tensorQuotEquivQuotSMul M J).symm
   112	      (Submodule.Quotient.mk x) = x ⊗ₜ[R] (1 : R ⧸ J) :=
   113	    TensorProduct.tensorQuotEquivQuotSMul_symm_mk J x
   114	  have h2 : (LinearMap.lTensor M (mapQSMul I a)) (x ⊗ₜ[R] (1 : R ⧸ J))
   115	      = x ⊗ₜ[R] (Submodule.Quotient.mk a : R ⧸ I) := by
   116	    rw [LinearMap.lTensor_tmul]
   117	    congr 1
   118	    rw [show (1 : R ⧸ J) = Submodule.Quotient.mk (1 : R) from rfl, mapQSMul_mk, mul_one]
   119	  have h3 : (TensorProduct.tensorQuotEquivQuotSMul M I)
   120	      (x ⊗ₜ[R] (Submodule.Quotient.mk a : R ⧸ I)) = Submodule.Quotient.mk (a • x) :=
   121	    TensorProduct.tensorQuotEquivQuotSMul_tmul_mk I x a
   122	  -- the middle image vanishes
   123	  have h4 : (LinearMap.lTensor M (mapQSMul I a)) (x ⊗ₜ[R] (1 : R ⧸ J)) = 0 := by
   124	    rw [h2]
   125	    apply (TensorProduct.tensorQuotEquivQuotSMul M I).injective
   126	    rw [h3, map_zero, Submodule.Quotient.mk_eq_zero]
   127	    exact h
   128	  -- flatness: the middle map is injective, so the left input vanishes
   129	  have h5 : (x ⊗ₜ[R] (1 : R ⧸ J) : M ⊗[R] (R ⧸ J)) = 0 :=
   130	    Module.Flat.lTensor_preserves_injective_linearMap (mapQSMul I a)
   131	      (mapQSMul_injective I a) (by rw [h4, map_zero])
   132	  have hmk : (Submodule.Quotient.mk x : M ⧸ (J • (⊤ : Submodule R M))) = 0 :=
   133	    (TensorProduct.tensorQuotEquivQuotSMul M J).symm.injective
   134	      (by rw [h1, h5, map_zero])
   135	  rwa [Submodule.Quotient.mk_eq_zero] at hmk
   136	
   137	end ColonLemma

   141	variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R] {M : Type v} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
   142	
   143	/-- Elements of `p • ⊤` die in the residue-field fibre: `x ∈ p•⊤ ⟹ x ⊗ 1 = 0` in
   144	`M ⊗[R] κ(p)`. (No flatness.) -/
   145	theorem tmul_residueField_one_eq_zero_of_mem_smul_top (p : Ideal R) [p.IsPrime] {x : M}
   146	    (hx : x ∈ p • (⊤ : Submodule R M)) :
   147	    (x ⊗ₜ[R] (1 : p.ResidueField) : M ⊗[R] p.ResidueField) = 0 := by
   148	  refine Submodule.smul_induction_on hx (fun r hr m _ => ?_) (fun y z hy hz => ?_)
   149	  · rw [TensorProduct.smul_tmul]
   150	    have h1 : r • (1 : p.ResidueField) = algebraMap R p.ResidueField r := by
   151	      rw [Algebra.smul_def, mul_one]
   152	    rw [h1, Ideal.algebraMap_residueField_eq_zero.mpr hr, TensorProduct.tmul_zero]
   153	  · rw [TensorProduct.add_tmul, hy, hz, add_zero]
   154	
   155	/-- **The prime-fibre kernel computation** (the flat half): for flat `M` and a prime
   156	`p`, `x ⊗ 1 = 0` in `M ⊗[R] κ(p)` forces `x ∈ p • ⊤`. The map
   157	`M ⧸ p•⊤ ≃ M ⊗ (R⧸p) → M ⊗ κ(p)` is injective because `R⧸p ↪ κ(p)` is and `M` is
   158	flat. -/
   159	theorem Module.Flat.mem_smul_top_of_tmul_residueField_one_eq_zero [Module.Flat R M]
   160	    (p : Ideal R) [p.IsPrime] {x : M}
   161	    (hx : (x ⊗ₜ[R] (1 : p.ResidueField) : M ⊗[R] p.ResidueField) = 0) :
   162	    x ∈ p • (⊤ : Submodule R M) := by
   163	  set f : (R ⧸ p) →ₗ[R] p.ResidueField :=
   164	    (Algebra.linearMap (R ⧸ p) p.ResidueField).restrictScalars R with hf
   165	  have hfinj : Function.Injective f := by
   166	    intro u v huv
   167	    exact Ideal.injective_algebraMap_quotient_residueField p huv
   168	  have h1 : (TensorProduct.tensorQuotEquivQuotSMul M p).symm
   169	      (Submodule.Quotient.mk x) = x ⊗ₜ[R] (1 : R ⧸ p) :=
   170	    TensorProduct.tensorQuotEquivQuotSMul_symm_mk p x
   171	  have h2 : (LinearMap.lTensor M f) (x ⊗ₜ[R] (1 : R ⧸ p))
   172	      = x ⊗ₜ[R] (1 : p.ResidueField) := by
   173	    rw [LinearMap.lTensor_tmul]
   174	    congr 1
   175	    rw [hf]
   176	    simp
   177	  have h5 : (x ⊗ₜ[R] (1 : R ⧸ p) : M ⊗[R] (R ⧸ p)) = 0 :=
   178	    Module.Flat.lTensor_preserves_injective_linearMap f hfinj
   179	      (by rw [h2, hx, map_zero])
   180	  have hmk : (Submodule.Quotient.mk x : M ⧸ (p • (⊤ : Submodule R M))) = 0 :=
   181	    (TensorProduct.tensorQuotEquivQuotSMul M p).symm.injective
   182	      (by rw [h1, h5, map_zero])
   183	  rwa [Submodule.Quotient.mk_eq_zero] at hmk
   184	
   185	end ResidueFibre

   191	/-- **The `lm:ctn`-lite slicing criterion, endomorphism form** (Kleiman `lm:ctn`
   192	(iii)⟹(i), Tor-free; DAT-A2 core): over a Noetherian ring `R`, an `R`-linear

   203	    intro I₀

   206	        φ x ∈ I • (⊤ : Submodule R M) → x ∈ I • (⊤ : Submodule R M))

   209	    by_cases htop : I = ⊤
   210	    · rw [htop, Submodule.top_smul]
   211	      exact Submodule.mem_top

   213	    · -- the prime case: the fibre hypothesis, no inductive hypothesis

   216	          (x ⊗ₜ[R] (1 : Ideal.ResidueField I)) = 0 := by
   217	        rw [LinearMap.rTensor_tmul]
   218	        exact tmul_residueField_one_eq_zero_of_mem_smul_top I hx
   219	      have h2 : (x ⊗ₜ[R] (1 : Ideal.ResidueField I) :
   220	          M ⊗[R] Ideal.ResidueField I) = 0 :=

   222	/-- The `j`-th **component** of a global section of the datum's glued sheaf, as a
   223	section of the trivializing basic-open piece `D(h_j)` (the `⊤ ⊓ pieces j`-to-`pieces j`

   229	/-- Every piece of the pinned datum is an affine open (a basic open of a pinned affine
   230	chart). -/
   231	theorem isAffineOpen_pieces (j : D.index) : IsAffineOpen (D.pieces j) := by
   232	  cases j with
   233	  | inl j₀ => exact (relCover_isAffineOpen₀ C B (fiberTwoCover π)).basicOpen (D.h₀ j₀)
   234	  | inr j₁ => exact (relCover_isAffineOpen₁ C B (fiberTwoCover π)).basicOpen (D.h₁ j₁)

   238	variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite π]

   241	/-- **DAT-A2 on the datum, section-ring form**: a fibrewise-regular component of a
   242	global section of the DAT-1 glued sheaf is a nonzerodivisor of its piece ring
   243	(fibrewise-regular + flat ⟹ regular; the chart rings are free `B`-modules by
   244	`free_relSections`, so the pieces are flat, and the `lm:ctn`-lite core fires). -/
   245	theorem component_mem_nonZeroDivisors [IsNoetherianRing B]
   246	    (s : ↥(gluedSubmodule B D.pieces D.unit ⊤)) (j : D.index)
   247	    (hfib : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum B, Function.Injective
   248	      ((Scheme.mulSectionEnd B (D.component s j)).rTensor p.asIdeal.ResidueField)) :
   249	    D.component s j ∈ nonZeroDivisors Γ(relCurve C B, D.pieces j) := by
   250	  cases j with
   251	  | inl j₀ =>
   252	      haveI : Module.Free B Γ(relCurve C B, (relCover C B (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀) :=
   253	        free_relSections C B (fiberChart₀ π)
   254	          (isAffineOpen_preimage_chartOpen π 0).isCompact
   255	          (isAffineOpen_preimage_chartOpen π 0).isQuasiSeparated
   256	      exact mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_fibrewise_regular B
   257	        (relCover_isAffineOpen₀ C B (fiberTwoCover π)) (D.h₀ j₀)
   258	        Module.Flat.of_free (D.component s (Sum.inl j₀)) hfib
   259	  | inr j₁ =>
   260	      haveI : Module.Free B Γ(relCurve C B, (relCover C B (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁) :=
   261	        free_relSections C B (fiberChart₁ π)
   262	          (isAffineOpen_preimage_chartOpen π 1).isCompact
   263	          (isAffineOpen_preimage_chartOpen π 1).isQuasiSeparated
   264	      exact mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_fibrewise_regular B
   265	        (relCover_isAffineOpen₁ C B (fiberTwoCover π)) (D.h₁ j₁)
   266	        Module.Flat.of_free (D.component s (Sum.inr j₁)) hfib
   267	
   268	/-- **DAT-A2 on the datum, germ form** (the `Scheme.LocalEquations.regular` input): a
   269	fibrewise-regular component has nonzerodivisor germs at every point of its piece. -/
   270	theorem germ_component_mem_nonZeroDivisors [IsNoetherianRing B]
   271	    (s : ↥(gluedSubmodule B D.pieces D.unit ⊤)) (j : D.index)
   272	    (hfib : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum B, Function.Injective
   273	      ((Scheme.mulSectionEnd B (D.component s j)).rTensor p.asIdeal.ResidueField))
   274	    (y : ↑(relCurve C B).toPresheafedSpace) (hy : y ∈ D.pieces j) :
   275	    ((relCurve C B).presheaf.germ (D.pieces j) y hy).hom (D.component s j)
   276	      ∈ nonZeroDivisors ((relCurve C B).presheaf.stalk y) :=
   277	  (D.isAffineOpen_pieces j).germ_mem_nonZeroDivisors
   278	    (D.component_mem_nonZeroDivisors s j hfib) y hy

    11	/-!
    12	# Chart-module structure of the m-chart glued sheaf (DAT-1, stage 1c)
    13	
    14	The `Γ(X, V)`-module and coefficient-ring properties of the glued section module
    15	`F(V)` on an affine chart `V` carrying a finite subordinate trivializing basic-open
    16	family (`informal/spec-dat-1.md`, decision (D5)): sections `h : ι → Γ(X, V)` whose
    17	basic opens `D(h i)` lie in gluing pieces (`hP : D(h i) ≤ U (σ i)`) and span the unit
    18	ideal (`hspan : Ideal.span (Set.range h) = ⊤` — the worksheet partition witness feeds
    19	this through `Ideal.span_range_eq_top_of_sum_eq_one`).
    20	
    21	All statements are relative to an ambient packaging
    22	`[Scheme.QcohOn (gluedSheaf k U g) V]` whose action is componentwise (the hypothesis
    23	`hq`, discharged by `rfl` for packagings built by `gluedQcohOn` — the same interface as
    24	`gluedPairData`), with the chart module structure `Scheme.QcohOn.moduleOfLE` bound by
    25	`letI` in statements (RE-0 pattern) and the section modules in the sheaf-object
    26	spelling `(gluedSheaf k U g).obj.obj (op W)` — the spelling the engine consumes.
    27	
    28	* `gluedPieceModule`/`gluedPieceEquiv` — each piece `F(D(h i))` is a free rank-one
    29	  `Γ(X, D(h i))`-module through the piece trivialization `gluedTriv`;
    30	* `isUnit_algebraMap_end_glued` — a chart section restricting to a unit acts invertibly
    31	  on the glued sections of an open below a piece (trivialization conjugation);
    32	* `isLocalizedModule_secResₗ_glued` — **the RE-0 bridge fired per piece**:
    33	  `F(V) → F(D(h i))` is an `IsLocalizedModule (Submonoid.powers (h i))` (the abstract
    34	  bridge at `V ⊓ D(h i)`, transported across the opens equality `V ⊓ D(h i) = D(h i)`
    35	  by `IsLocalizedModule.of_linearEquiv`);
    36	* the localization-local chart properties: `moduleFinite_glued`,
    37	  `finitePresentation_glued`, `flat_glued`, `projective_glued` (over `Γ(X, V)`), and
    38	  the coefficient-ring transports `flat_glued_of_flat` (under `Module.Flat k Γ(X, V)` —
    39	  a benign weakening of the spec's freeness hypothesis: free ⟹ flat) and
    40	  `projective_glued_of_free` (under `Module.Free k Γ(X, V)`);
    41	* `moduleFinite_aeval'_glued` — the `AEval'`-finiteness export: an endomorphism acting
    42	  as the packaged action of a chart coordinate `a₀` has `k[X]`-finite chart lattice
    43	  whenever `Scheme.mulSectionEnd k a₀` does (the landed E-i input), through
    44	  `RigidEngine.moduleFinite_aeval'_of_smul_finite` and `moduleFinite_glued`.
    45	-/

    53	/-! ## A partition of unity spans the unit ideal -/
    54	
    55	/-- **Span-⊤ from a partition of unity**: if `∑ i, a i * h i = 1` in a commutative ring,
    56	the range of `h` generates the unit ideal. -/
    57	theorem Ideal.span_range_eq_top_of_sum_eq_one {A : Type u} [CommRing A] {ι : Type*}
    58	    [Fintype ι] (a h : ι → A) (hpart : ∑ i, a i * h i = 1) :
    59	    Ideal.span (Set.range h) = ⊤ := by
    60	  rw [Ideal.eq_top_iff_one, ← hpart]
    61	  exact Ideal.sum_mem _ fun i _ =>
    62	    Ideal.mul_mem_left _ _ (Ideal.subset_span (Set.mem_range_self i))

    74	/-! ## Restriction bookkeeping -/
    75	
    76	/-- Componentwise restriction composes. -/
    77	lemma gluedRes_gluedRes {W'' W' W : X.Opens} (h₁ : W'' ≤ W') (h₂ : W' ≤ W)
    78	    (s : ↥(gluedSubmodule k U g W)) :
    79	    gluedRes k U g h₁ (gluedRes k U g h₂ s) = gluedRes k U g (h₁.trans h₂) s :=
    80	  Subtype.ext (funext fun _ => by
    81	    simp only [gluedRes_coe, Scheme.resHom_resHom])

    85	    gluedRes k U g hW s = s :=
    86	  Subtype.ext (funext fun _ => Scheme.resHom_self _ _)

    90	/-- The componentwise action of the image `X.overAlgebraMap k V c` of a coefficient
    91	`c : k` agrees with the `k`-module action on glued sections. -/
    92	lemma gluedQsmul_overAlgebraMap {V W : X.Opens} (hWV : W ≤ V) (c : k)

    95	  refine Subtype.ext (funext fun j => ?_)

   101	variable {V : X.Opens} {ι : Type u} {σ : ι → J} {h : ι → Γ(X, V)}
   102	
   103	/-! ## The piece module structure -/
   104	
   105	/-- **The `Aᵢ := Γ(X, D(h i))`-module structure on a piece** `Mᵢ := F(D(h i))`,
   106	transported through the `k`-linear piece trivialization `tᵢ : Mᵢ ≃ₗ[k] Γ(X, D(h i))`:
   107	`a • m := tᵢ⁻¹ (a * tᵢ m)`. This makes `Mᵢ` free of rank one over `Aᵢ`
   108	(`gluedPieceEquiv`). -/
   109	@[reducible] noncomputable def gluedPieceModule (hc : Scheme.IsGluingCocycle U g)
   110	    (hP : ∀ i : ι, X.basicOpen (h i) ≤ U (σ i)) (i : ι) :
   111	    Module Γ(X, X.basicOpen (h i)) ↥(gluedSubmodule k U g (X.basicOpen (h i))) where
   112	  smul a m := (gluedTriv k hc (σ i) (hP i)).symm (a * gluedTriv k hc (σ i) (hP i) m)
   113	  one_smul m := by
   114	    change (gluedTriv k hc (σ i) (hP i)).symm (1 * gluedTriv k hc (σ i) (hP i) m) = m
   115	    rw [one_mul, LinearEquiv.symm_apply_apply]
   116	  mul_smul a b m := by
   117	    change (gluedTriv k hc (σ i) (hP i)).symm (a * b * gluedTriv k hc (σ i) (hP i) m) =
   118	      (gluedTriv k hc (σ i) (hP i)).symm
   119	        (a * gluedTriv k hc (σ i) (hP i)
   120	          ((gluedTriv k hc (σ i) (hP i)).symm (b * gluedTriv k hc (σ i) (hP i) m)))
   121	    rw [LinearEquiv.apply_symm_apply, mul_assoc]
   122	  smul_zero a := by
   123	    change (gluedTriv k hc (σ i) (hP i)).symm (a * gluedTriv k hc (σ i) (hP i) 0) = 0
   124	    rw [map_zero, mul_zero, map_zero]
   125	  smul_add a m n := by
   126	    change (gluedTriv k hc (σ i) (hP i)).symm (a * gluedTriv k hc (σ i) (hP i) (m + n)) =
   127	      (gluedTriv k hc (σ i) (hP i)).symm (a * gluedTriv k hc (σ i) (hP i) m) +
   128	        (gluedTriv k hc (σ i) (hP i)).symm (a * gluedTriv k hc (σ i) (hP i) n)
   129	    rw [map_add, mul_add, map_add]
   130	  add_smul a b m := by
   131	    change (gluedTriv k hc (σ i) (hP i)).symm ((a + b) * gluedTriv k hc (σ i) (hP i) m) =
   132	      (gluedTriv k hc (σ i) (hP i)).symm (a * gluedTriv k hc (σ i) (hP i) m) +
   133	        (gluedTriv k hc (σ i) (hP i)).symm (b * gluedTriv k hc (σ i) (hP i) m)
   134	    rw [add_mul, map_add]
   135	  zero_smul m := by
   136	    change (gluedTriv k hc (σ i) (hP i)).symm (0 * gluedTriv k hc (σ i) (hP i) m) = 0
   137	    rw [zero_mul, map_zero]
   138	
   139	lemma gluedPieceModule_smul_def (hc : Scheme.IsGluingCocycle U g)
   140	    (hP : ∀ i : ι, X.basicOpen (h i) ≤ U (σ i)) (i : ι)
   141	    (a : Γ(X, X.basicOpen (h i))) (m : ↥(gluedSubmodule k U g (X.basicOpen (h i)))) :
   142	    letI := gluedPieceModule k U g hc hP i
   143	    a • m = (gluedTriv k hc (σ i) (hP i)).symm (a * gluedTriv k hc (σ i) (hP i) m) :=
   144	  rfl
   145	
   146	/-- **Each piece is `Aᵢ`-free of rank one**: the piece trivialization `tᵢ`, promoted to
   147	an `Aᵢ`-linear equivalence `Mᵢ ≃ₗ[Aᵢ] Aᵢ` for the `gluedPieceModule` structure. -/
   148	noncomputable def gluedPieceEquiv (hc : Scheme.IsGluingCocycle U g)
   149	    (hP : ∀ i : ι, X.basicOpen (h i) ≤ U (σ i)) (i : ι) :
   150	    letI := gluedPieceModule k U g hc hP i
   151	    ↥(gluedSubmodule k U g (X.basicOpen (h i))) ≃ₗ[Γ(X, X.basicOpen (h i))]
   152	      Γ(X, X.basicOpen (h i)) :=
   153	  letI := gluedPieceModule k U g hc hP i
   154	  { toFun := gluedTriv k hc (σ i) (hP i)
   155	    map_add' := (gluedTriv k hc (σ i) (hP i)).map_add
   156	    map_smul' := fun a m => by
   157	      change gluedTriv k hc (σ i) (hP i)
   158	          ((gluedTriv k hc (σ i) (hP i)).symm (a * gluedTriv k hc (σ i) (hP i) m)) =
   159	        a • gluedTriv k hc (σ i) (hP i) m
   160	      rw [LinearEquiv.apply_symm_apply, smul_eq_mul]
   161	    invFun := (gluedTriv k hc (σ i) (hP i)).symm
   162	    left_inv := (gluedTriv k hc (σ i) (hP i)).left_inv
   163	    right_inv := (gluedTriv k hc (σ i) (hP i)).right_inv }
   164	
   165	@[simp]
   166	lemma gluedPieceEquiv_apply (hc : Scheme.IsGluingCocycle U g)

     9	# The unconditional splitting of a plus class over a field (CHART-U(a), input 1)
    10	
    11	`informal/w4-datb-worksheet.md` §1.2 step 1 and `informal/w4-datc-worksheet.md` §3.3 both
    12	open with the same move, and both treat it as a step of a longer argument:
    13	
    14	> restrict along `t`; a plus class over `κ(t)` is `PicEtAff.mk E x`; étale field-cofinality
    15	> produces a finite separable `L/κ(t)` over which the class is an honest Čech class.
    16	
    17	This file makes that move a **named, unconditional theorem** rather than a step, because it
    18	is consumed at three separate places (the split predicate `IsSplitWitness`, the coverage
    19	theorem COV-1, and the degree seam) and because its statement is exactly the *witness-free*
    20	half of `IsSplitWitness`: every plus class over a field becomes an honest Čech class over
    21	some finite separable extension.  Nothing here mentions a witness divisor, `H¹`, `θ`, `Σ`,
    22	`divRep` or a certificate.
    23	
    24	## Why this is worth isolating
    25	
    26	`IsSplitWitness C μ` (`Picard/Pic0ChartLocus.lean:148`) is an existential over a *tuple*: the
    27	extension `L`, its four instances, the presenting Čech class `M`, and then the witness
    28	divisor.  Read naively, a consumer proving membership of `chartLocus` has to produce all of
    29	them at once, and a consumer *using* membership has to destructure all of them.  But the
    30	first six components exist for **every** class, with no hypothesis at all — that is
    31	`exists_splitting_of_picEt` below.  So the honest content of `IsSplitWitness` is only the
    32	witness clause *at* a splitting, and the two readings are related by
    33	`isSplitWitness_iff_exists_splitting_witness`.
    34	
    35	That matters for the lane order: COV-1 (dat-b §1.2) can produce its splitting *before* it
    36	knows anything about `h⁰`/`h¹`, choose `m` at that field (§1.2 step 3, where the uniform
    37	bound genuinely does not exist), and only then run the drop.  Without this separation the
    38	`m`-choice and the splitting choice are entangled inside one `∃`.
    39	
    40	## Main declarations
    41	
    42	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_splitting_of_picEtAff` — **every plus class over a field is an
    43	  honest Čech class over some finite separable extension.**  Unconditional; no witness.
    44	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_splitting_of_picEt` — the same in the `picEt` spelling, which is
    45	  the one `IsSplitWitness` is stated against.
    46	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isSplitWitness_iff_exists_splitting_witness` — the two readings agree:
    47	  `IsSplitWitness` is exactly "some splitting carries a witness".  Its `.mpr` is also the
    48	  introduction rule; see the closing note for why no positional constructor lemma exists.
    49	-/

   186	`IsSplitWitness` mixes the two spellings of the base-changed curve —
   187	`(relCurve C L).CechPic` for the presenting class, `((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).CurveDivisor` for
   188	the witness divisor — so a single tuple makes Lean unify the seven instance slots *while `L` is
   189	still a metavariable*, re-checking those carriers on each attempted assignment.  `refine`
   190	instead of `exact`, pre-bundling the witness clause, normalising either spelling, and routing
   191	through the `iff` are all the same shape, and all of them time out.
   192	
   193	What it got wrong was the conclusion drawn from that: it read "the tuple is too expensive" as
   194	"there is no introduction rule", and proposed restating `IsSplitWitness` with one spelling —
   195	a refactor of a definition co-signed in `w4-datb` §1.6.  The actual fix is tactic-level:
   196	**stage the existentials.**  Eight `refine Exists.intro x ?_`s fix `L` at the first step, after
   197	which every later component is checked against a closed type and the two spellings never race.
   198	
   199	So the corrected rule is not "prefer `Iff.rfl` plus `.mpr`" but: *a deep existential over
   200	types-carrying-instances must have its intros staged, not bundled.*  The diagnosis above is
   201	not refuted by this — it is precisely why staging works. -/
   202	
   203	end
   204	
   205	end AlgebraicGeometry

    10	/-!
    11	# Legal chart indices after finite base change
    12	
    13	This file supplies the positive replacement for a base-field genus divisor-degree assumption.
    14	Every challenge curve has a closed point; its residue field is a finite extension over which the
    15	curve has a rational point.  More strongly, a point over a separable closure spreads through the
    16	cofiltered limit of finite subextensions, producing a point over a finite separable extension.
    17	The graph of either point then produces a legal chart index at every natural parameter, in
    18	particular at the genus.  The stronger construction matters over imperfect fields: an arbitrary
    19	closed point can be inseparable even though smoothness guarantees that a separable one can be
    20	chosen.
    21	
    22	## Main declarations
    23	
    24	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_finite_point` — every challenge curve acquires a point over a
    25	  finite extension, obtained from a closed point and its residue field.
    26	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_finiteSubextension_point_of_point` — a point over an algebraic
    27	  extension of a finitely presented scheme spreads to one finite subextension.
    28	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_finite_separable_point` — every challenge curve acquires a point
    29	  over a finite separable extension, with no point or divisor-degree hypothesis.
    30	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_finite_galois_point` — normal closure upgrades this to a finite
    31	  Galois extension, still without a new curve hypothesis.
    32	* `AlgebraicGeometry.baseChangePoint` — the fibre-product lift of an extension-valued point to
    33	  a rational point of the base-changed curve.
    34	* `AlgebraicGeometry.overSpecFieldExtension_mem_fpqcTopology` — a field extension is an fpqc
    35	  singleton cover of the base field.
    36	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_fpqc_pointCover` — one finite fpqc cover carrying a point of the
    37	  curve.
    38	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_fpqc_chartIndices` — that same cover supports a legal chart index
    39	  at every natural parameter.
    40	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_galois_chartIndices` — the common cover can be chosen finite
    41	  Galois, in the form consumed by Galois descent.
    42	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_fpqc_chartIndex` — the finite cover and a legal chart index are
    43	  produced together.
    44	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_finite_chartIndex` — every natural parameter has a legal
    45	  chart index after one finite base change.
    46	-/
    47

    61	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    62	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    63	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
