    67	variable (C) in
    68	/-- Every challenge curve acquires a rational point over a finite extension.
    69	
    70	Choose a closed point of the integral Jacobson scheme `C`.  Its residue field is finite over
    71	`k` because the corresponding point morphism is finite.  The canonical residue-field point then
    72	gives the required morphism.  In particular, this is a producer from the standing curve
    73	assumptions, not a new point hypothesis. -/
    74	theorem exists_finite_point :
    75	    ∃ (L : Type u) (_ : Field L) (_ : Algebra k L)
    76	      (_ : Module.Finite k L),
    77	      Nonempty (overSpec k L ⟶ C) := by
    78	  haveI : IsIntegral C.left := isIntegral_left_of_geometricallyReduced C
    79	  haveI : JacobsonSpace C.left := LocallyOfFiniteType.jacobsonSpace C.hom
    80	  obtain ⟨x, _, hx⟩ := nonempty_inter_closedPoints
    81	    (Z := (Set.univ : Set C.left)) Set.univ_nonempty isOpen_univ.isLocallyClosed
    82	  have hxclosed : IsClosed ({x} : Set C.left) := mem_closedPoints_iff.mp hx
    83	  let L := Over.testPointField x
    84	  letI : Field L := inferInstance
    85	  letI : Algebra k L := inferInstance
    86	  haveI hfinite : Module.Finite k L := by
    87	    haveI : LocallyOfFiniteType (C.left.fromSpecResidueField x) :=
    88	      isClosed_singleton_iff_locallyOfFiniteType.mp hxclosed
    89	    haveI : LocallyOfFiniteType
    90	        (C.left.fromSpecResidueField x ≫ C.hom) := inferInstance
    91	    haveI : IsFinite (C.left.fromSpecResidueField x ≫ C.hom) :=
    92	      isFinite_iff_locallyOfFiniteType_of_jacobsonSpace.mpr inferInstance
    93	    rw [← RingHom.finite_algebraMap]
    94	    apply (IsFinite.SpecMap_iff _).mp
    95	    rw [Spec.map_preimage]
    96	    exact inferInstance
    97	  exact ⟨L, inferInstance, inferInstance, hfinite, ⟨Over.testPoint x⟩⟩
    98	
    99	omit [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
   100	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] in
   101	/-- The identity of `Spec L`, typed from the `L`-relative affine test to the same affine
   102	scheme regarded as a `k`-relative test. -/
   103	noncomputable def overSpecLeftChangeBase (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L] :
   104	    (overSpec L L).left ⟶ (overSpec k L).left :=
   105	  𝟙 (Spec (.of L))
   106	
   107	omit [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
   108	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] in
   109	/-- The change-of-base identity is the structure morphism of `overSpec L L`. -/
   110	lemma overSpecLeftChangeBase_eq (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L] :
   111	    overSpecLeftChangeBase (k := k) L = (overSpec L L).hom := by
   112	  change 𝟙 (Spec (.of L)) = (overSpec L L).hom
   113	  exact overSpec_self_hom.symm
   114	
   115	omit [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
   116	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] in
   117	variable (C) in
   118	/-- A point of `C` over an extension field `L` is canonically an `L`-rational point of the
   119	base-changed curve.  Its underlying morphism is the lift of the point and the identity of
   120	`Spec L` into the defining fibre product. -/
   121	noncomputable def baseChangePoint {L : Type u} [Field L] [Algebra k L]
   122	    (p : overSpec k L ⟶ C) : overSpec L L ⟶ baseChangeBundle C L :=
   123	  show overSpec L L ⟶ Over.mk (pullback.snd C.hom (overSpec k L).hom) from
   124	    Over.homMk
   125	      (pullback.lift (overSpecLeftChangeBase (k := k) L ≫ p.left)
   126	        (overSpecLeftChangeBase (k := k) L) (by rw [Category.assoc, p.w]))
   127	      ((pullback.lift_snd _ _ _).trans (overSpecLeftChangeBase_eq (k := k) L))
   128	
   129	omit [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
   130	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] in
   131	variable (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L] in
   132	/-- The spectrum map of a field extension is surjective. -/
   133	instance instSurjectiveOverSpecFieldExtension : Surjective (overSpec k L).hom := by
   134	  rw [overSpec_hom]
   135	  apply ((flat_and_surjective_SpecMap_iff
   136	    (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k L))).mpr ?_).2
   137	  rw [CommRingCat.hom_ofHom, RingHom.faithfullyFlat_algebraMap_iff]
   138	  infer_instance
   139	
   140	omit [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
   141	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] in
   142	variable (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L] in
   143	/-- A field extension gives a singleton fpqc cover of the base field. -/
   144	theorem overSpecFieldExtension_mem_fpqcTopology :
   145	    Sieve.generate (Presieve.singleton (overSpec k L).hom) ∈
   146	      Scheme.fpqcTopology (Spec (.of k)) :=
   147	  Precoverage.generate_mem_toGrothendieck
   148	    (overSpec k L).hom.singleton_mem_fpqcPrecoverage
   149	
   150	variable (C) in
   151	/-- Every challenge curve has a point on one finite fpqc cover of the base field. -/
   152	theorem exists_fpqc_pointCover :
   153	    ∃ (L : Type u) (_ : Field L) (_ : Algebra k L)
   154	      (_ : Module.Finite k L),
   155	      Sieve.generate (Presieve.singleton (overSpec k L).hom) ∈
   156	          Scheme.fpqcTopology (Spec (.of k)) ∧
   157	        Nonempty (overSpec k L ⟶ C) := by
   158	  obtain ⟨L, hLfield, hkL, hfinite, hp⟩ := exists_finite_point C
   159	  letI : Field L := hLfield
   160	  letI : Algebra k L := hkL
   161	  letI : Module.Finite k L := hfinite
   162	  exact ⟨L, inferInstance, inferInstance, inferInstance,
   163	    overSpecFieldExtension_mem_fpqcTopology (k := k) L, hp⟩
   164	
   165	variable (C) in
   166	/-- One finite fpqc cover supports legal chart indices at every natural parameter.
   167	
   168	Unlike `exists_fpqc_chartIndex`, the extension is chosen outside the parameter quantifier.  A
   169	mixed-parameter atlas can therefore use one cover for its entire chart family. -/
   170	theorem exists_fpqc_chartIndices :
   171	    ∃ (L : Type u) (_ : Field L) (_ : Algebra k L)
   172	      (_ : Module.Finite k L),
   173	      Sieve.generate (Presieve.singleton (overSpec k L).hom) ∈
   174	          Scheme.fpqcTopology (Spec (.of k)) ∧
   175	        ∀ n : ℕ, ∃ (m : ℕ)
   176	          (Z : ((baseChangeBundle C L) ⊗ overSpec L L).left.CurveDivisor),
   177	          Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg L Z =
   178	            (m : ℤ) * classDeg L (thetaCechClass (baseChangeBundle C L)) - (n : ℤ) := by
   179	  obtain ⟨L, hLfield, hkL, hfinite, hcover, ⟨p⟩⟩ := exists_fpqc_pointCover C
   180	  letI : Field L := hLfield
   181	  letI : Algebra k L := hkL
   182	  letI : Module.Finite k L := hfinite
   183	  exact ⟨L, inferInstance, inferInstance, inferInstance, hcover,
   184	    fun n => exists_chartIndex_of_point (baseChangeBundle C L) (baseChangePoint C p) n⟩
   185	
   186	variable (C) in
   187	/-- One finite Galois cover supports legal chart indices at every natural parameter.
   188	
   189	The normal-closure producer supplies the extension and its curve point.  Field-extension
   190	coverhood is fpqc independently of Galoisness, while the `IsGalois` instance makes this package
   191	directly usable by quotient/descent constructions indexed by `Gal(L/k)`. -/
   192	theorem exists_galois_chartIndices :
   193	    ∃ (L : Type u) (_ : Field L) (_ : Algebra k L)
   194	      (_ : Module.Finite k L) (_ : IsGalois k L),
   195	      Sieve.generate (Presieve.singleton (overSpec k L).hom) ∈
   196	          Scheme.fpqcTopology (Spec (.of k)) ∧
   197	        ∀ n : ℕ, ∃ (m : ℕ)
   198	          (Z : ((baseChangeBundle C L) ⊗ overSpec L L).left.CurveDivisor),
   199	          Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg L Z =
   200	            (m : ℤ) * classDeg L (thetaCechClass (baseChangeBundle C L)) - (n : ℤ) := by
   201	  obtain ⟨L, hLfield, hkL, hfinite, hgalois, ⟨p⟩⟩ := exists_finite_galois_point C
   202	  letI : Field L := hLfield
   203	  letI : Algebra k L := hkL
   204	  letI : Module.Finite k L := hfinite
   205	  letI : IsGalois k L := hgalois
   206	  exact ⟨L, inferInstance, inferInstance, inferInstance, inferInstance,
   207	    overSpecFieldExtension_mem_fpqcTopology (k := k) L,
   208	    fun n => exists_chartIndex_of_point (baseChangeBundle C L) (baseChangePoint C p) n⟩
   209	
   210	variable (C) in
   211	/-- Every natural chart parameter becomes legal on a finite fpqc cover.
   212	
   213	The cover and the chart index are returned in one package.  This is the producer-facing form
   214	for descent: the caller does not need to recover fpqc coverhood from the finite field extension. -/
   215	theorem exists_fpqc_chartIndex (n : ℕ) :
   216	    ∃ (L : Type u) (_ : Field L) (_ : Algebra k L)
   217	      (_ : Module.Finite k L),
   218	      Sieve.generate (Presieve.singleton (overSpec k L).hom) ∈
   219	          Scheme.fpqcTopology (Spec (.of k)) ∧
   220	        ∃ (m : ℕ)
   221	          (Z : ((baseChangeBundle C L) ⊗ overSpec L L).left.CurveDivisor),
   222	          Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg L Z =
   223	            (m : ℤ) * classDeg L (thetaCechClass (baseChangeBundle C L)) - (n : ℤ) := by
   224	  obtain ⟨L, hLfield, hkL, hfinite, hcover, hindices⟩ := exists_fpqc_chartIndices C
   225	  exact ⟨L, hLfield, hkL, hfinite, hcover, hindices n⟩
   226	
   227	variable (C) in
   228	/-- Every natural chart parameter becomes legal after one finite base change.
   229	
   230	The extension is produced by `exists_finite_point`; no divisor-degree or rational-point
   231	assumption is added.  This is the positive input for constructing genus charts over a cover
   232	before descending the resulting restricted atlas to the base field. -/
   233	theorem exists_finite_chartIndex (n : ℕ) :
   234	    ∃ (L : Type u) (_ : Field L) (_ : Algebra k L)
   235	      (_ : Module.Finite k L),
   236	      ∃ (m : ℕ)
   237	        (Z : ((baseChangeBundle C L) ⊗ overSpec L L).left.CurveDivisor),
   238	        Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg L Z =
   239	          (m : ℤ) * classDeg L (thetaCechClass (baseChangeBundle C L)) - (n : ℤ) := by
   240	  obtain ⟨L, hLfield, hkL, hfinite, _, hindex⟩ := exists_fpqc_chartIndex C n
   241	  exact ⟨L, hLfield, hkL, hfinite, hindex⟩
   242	
   243	end

     9	# CHART-U(b) gap-2, the chartLocus-free core — fibre-field invariance of witness
    10	h¹-vanishing (`informal/w4-datb-worksheet.md` §1.6 transport (ii), I-0252 gap 2)
    11	
    12	CHART-U(b)'s transport (ii) (the "one `IsOpenMap` application", `Pic0ChartLocusOpen`
    13	keystones 2/3) pushes the engine's open witness locus from the étale carrier `Spec B`
    14	down to the test base `Spec A`.  Its remaining mathematical content (I-0252 gap 2) is
    15	the *fibre-field invariance* that identifies the preimage of the base locus with the
    16	carrier locus: for a prime `q` of the carrier over `p`, the residue-field extension
    17	`κ(q)/κ(p)` is separable (étale/étale-plus carrier) and must **preserve** the witness
    18	h¹-vanishing of the fibre class.
    19	
    20	That content is `chartLocus`-free (I-0252's phrasing through the still-undefined
    21	`chartLocus`, DAT-C C9, is pure plumbing on top) and is landed here in the **witness
    22	form** `BasicOpenCocycleDatum.isOpen_setOf_exists_witness_h1_vanishing`
    23	(`Pic0ChartLocusOpen`) uses.  The heart is a single module fact:
    24	
    25	* `AlgebraicGeometry.subsingleton_tensorProduct_field_ext_iff` — for an `S`-module `H`
    26	  and a field extension `L → L'` in the `S`-tower, `H ⊗[S] L` is subsingleton iff
    27	  `H ⊗[S] L'` is.  Going up is `0 ⊗ = 0`; coming down is the faithful flatness of the
    28	  (nonzero) field extension.  **Separability is not needed** — every field extension is
    29	  faithfully flat; it is the geometric packaging (étale carrier) that makes the residue
    30	  extensions separable, not the transfer.
    31	
    32	Read through the two-way datum dictionary
    33	`BasicOpenCocycleDatum.subsingleton_h1_tensor_iff_exists_witness` (C1, GAP-6) — under
    34	which the witness predicate at a field `L` is exactly the engine's complex-form fibre
    35	condition `Subsingleton ((datumPair D).H1 ⊗[B] L)` — this gives:
    36	
    37	* `BasicOpenCocycleDatum.HasWitnessH1Vanishing` — the field-parametrised witness
    38	  predicate; for `L = κ(q)` it is membership of `q` in the keystone-1 locus.
    39	* `BasicOpenCocycleDatum.hasWitnessH1Vanishing_iff_of_fieldExtension` — **the gap-2
    40	  core**: witness h¹-vanishing of `D` at `L` transfers to and from `L'` for any field
    41	  extension `L → L'` in the `k`/`B` tower.
    42	* `BasicOpenCocycleDatum.hasWitnessH1Vanishing_iff_of_separable` — the separable
    43	  specialisation the CHART-U(b) consumer names (`Algebra.IsSeparable`).
    44	* `BasicOpenCocycleDatum.hasWitnessH1Vanishing_congr_of_cechPicClass_eq` — the fixed-
    45	  field class-intrinsicity (V1a): the witness predicate depends only on the mapped fibre
    46	  class, so two data with equal fibre class at `L` have the same predicate.
    47	
    48	## What the CHART-U(b) / C9 assembly consumes and the residual (I-0252 gap 2)

    10	/-!
    11	# The widened divisor representer at the Picard atlas seam
    12	
    13	The widened divisor functor of a challenge curve is represented at the genus parameter.  This
    14	module inserts that representation into the Abel construction and then into the Zariski-local
    15	representability theorem for the degree-zero Picard functor.
    16	
    17	The resulting chart family has no assumed divisor representation.  Its remaining inputs are the
    18	two geometric conditions of the local-representability theorem: every restricted Abel map is a
    19	representable open immersion, and the restricted maps cover the Picard sheaf pointwise.
    20	
    21	This is not an unconditional Picard representability result: the final declaration below retains
    22	both geometric inputs.  Moreover, at the larger admissible coverage parameter the raw Abel map has
    23	positive-dimensional linear-system fibres in positive genus, so the larger divisor representer
    24	cannot simply be substituted as an open chart source.  The remaining datum-tail construction is
    25	the corrected Altman--Kleiman step: represent the quotient by equality of the induced Picard class,
    26	thereby removing those fibres before applying the Picard representability seam.
    27	
    28	## Main declarations
    29	
    30	* `AlgebraicGeometry.abelSigmaChartAffGenus` is the widened Abel chart formed from the chosen
    31	  genus-parameter divisor representer.
    32	* `AlgebraicGeometry.universalDivFamAffGenus` is its universal widened divisor family.
    33	* `AlgebraicGeometry.abelSigmaChartAffAdmissible` is the no-argument widened Abel map at the
    34	  unconditional admissible coverage parameter; its legal chart index is chosen internally.
    35	* `AlgebraicGeometry.universalDivFamAffAdmissible` is the corresponding universal family.
    36	* `AlgebraicGeometry.affineGenusChart` restricts a multi-index family of these maps to chosen
    37	  source opens.
    38	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0RepresentableByOfAffineGenusCharts` is the conditional final assembly
    39	  once the restricted charts are open immersions and cover pointwise.
    40	-/
    41	
    42	set_option autoImplicit false
    43	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
    44	
    45	universe u
    46	
    47	open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory Opposite
    48	
    49	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    50	
    51	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    52	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    53	variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    54	
    55	noncomputable section
    56	
    57	/-- The universal widened divisor family carried by the chosen genus-parameter representer. -/
    58	def universalDivFamAffGenus :
    59	    divFamZarAff C (genus C) (divRepAffGenusScheme C) :=
    60	  (divFunctorAff_genus_representableBy C).homEquiv (𝟙 _)
    61	
    62	/-- Pulling back the chosen universal family gives the widened family classified by the
    63	corresponding morphism into the genus representer. -/
    64	theorem universalDivFamAffGenus_map {T : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    65	    (q : T ⟶ divRepAffGenusScheme C) :
    66	    divFamZarAff.map C (genus C) q (universalDivFamAffGenus C)
    67	      = (divFunctorAff_genus_representableBy C).homEquiv q := by
    68	  have h := (divFunctorAff_genus_representableBy C).homEquiv_comp q
    69	    (𝟙 (divRepAffGenusScheme C))
    70	  rw [Category.comp_id] at h
    71	  exact h.symm
    72	
    73	/-- The universal widened divisor family carried by the unconditional representer at the
    74	admissible coverage parameter. -/
    75	def universalDivFamAffAdmissible :
    76	    divFamZarAff C (divRepAffAdmissibleParameter C) (divRepAffAdmissibleScheme C) :=
    77	  (divFunctorAff_admissible_representableBy C).homEquiv (𝟙 _)
    78	
    79	/-- Pullback of the admissible universal family agrees with classification by the unconditional
    80	admissible representer. -/
    81	theorem universalDivFamAffAdmissible_map {T : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    82	    (q : T ⟶ divRepAffAdmissibleScheme C) :
    83	    divFamZarAff.map C (divRepAffAdmissibleParameter C) q
    84	        (universalDivFamAffAdmissible C)
    85	      = (divFunctorAff_admissible_representableBy C).homEquiv q := by
    86	  have h := (divFunctorAff_admissible_representableBy C).homEquiv_comp q
    87	    (𝟙 (divRepAffAdmissibleScheme C))
    88	  rw [Category.comp_id] at h
    89	  exact h.symm
    90	
    91	/-- The widened Abel chart at the genus parameter, using the challenge curve's chosen divisor
    92	representer rather than accepting a representability witness as an argument. -/
    93	def abelSigmaChartAffGenus
    94	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
    95	    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
    96	      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (genus C : ℤ)) :
    97	    yoneda.obj (divRepAffGenusScheme C).left ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1 :=
    98	  abelSigmaChartAff C (genus C) (divFunctorAff_genus_representableBy C) m Z hdeg
    99	
   100	attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra in
   101	attribute [local instance 10000] relCurve.instOver in
   102	/-- The widened Abel map at the unconditional admissible coverage parameter.  A legal chart
   103	index whose locus is universal is chosen internally; this declaration does not assert that the
   104	raw Abel map is an open immersion or an atlas. -/
   105	def abelSigmaChartAffAdmissible :
   106	    yoneda.obj (divRepAffAdmissibleScheme C).left ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1 := by
   107	  classical
   108	  letI : C.left.Over (Spec (.of k)) := .ofHom C.hom
   109	  haveI : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (C.left ↘ Spec (.of k)) :=
   110	    inferInstanceAs (SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom)
   111	  haveI : IsIntegral C.left := isIntegral_left_of_geometricallyReduced C
   112	  haveI : LocallyOfFiniteType (C.left ↘ Spec (.of k)) :=
   113	    inferInstanceAs (LocallyOfFiniteType C.hom)
   114	  haveI : QuasiCompact (C.left ↘ Spec (.of k)) :=
   115	    inferInstanceAs (QuasiCompact C.hom)
   116	  haveI : Module.Finite k (Sheaf.HModule (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) 0) :=
   117	    moduleFinite_hModule_zero C
   118	  haveI : Module.Finite k (Sheaf.HModule (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) 1) :=
   119	    moduleFinite_hModule_one C
   120	  let hchart := exists_uniform_admissibleCoverageChart_eq_univ
   121	    (C := C) (divRepAffP1Map_comp C) (genus C) (chi_moduleKSheaf C)
   122	  let m : ℕ := Classical.choose hchart
   123	  let hZ := Classical.choose_spec hchart
   124	  let Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor := Classical.choose hZ
   125	  have hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
   126	      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C)
   127	        - (divRepAffAdmissibleParameter C : ℤ) := by
   128	    change Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
   129	      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C)
   130	        - (admissibleCoverageParameter
   131	            (C := C) (divRepAffP1Map_comp C) (genus C) : ℤ)
   132	    exact (Classical.choose_spec hZ).1
   133	  exact abelSigmaChartAff C (divRepAffAdmissibleParameter C)
   134	    (divFunctorAff_admissible_representableBy C) m Z hdeg

   136	/-- The structure morphism read from a genus-parameter widened Abel chart is the structure
   137	morphism of the chosen divisor representer. -/
   138	lemma chartHom_abelSigmaChartAffGenus
   139	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
   140	    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
   141	      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (genus C : ℤ))
   142	    {ι : Type u} (i : ι) :
   143	    chartHom C (fun _ : ι => abelSigmaChartAffGenus C m Z hdeg) i
   144	      = (divRepAffGenusScheme C).hom :=
   145	  chartHom_abelSigmaChartAff (divFunctorAff_genus_representableBy C) m Z hdeg i
   146	
   147	/-- The structure morphism read from the admissible Abel map is the structure morphism of the
   148	unconditional admissible divisor representer. -/
   149	lemma chartHom_abelSigmaChartAffAdmissible {ι : Type u} (i : ι) :
   150	    chartHom C (fun _ : ι => abelSigmaChartAffAdmissible C) i
   151	      = (divRepAffAdmissibleScheme C).hom := by
   152	  dsimp only [abelSigmaChartAffAdmissible]
   153	  exact chartHom_abelSigmaChartAff
   154	    (divFunctorAff_admissible_representableBy C) _ _ _ i
   155	
   156	/-- A multi-index family of genus-parameter widened Abel charts, restricted to source opens.
   157	Different indices may use different twists and different opens, but they all use the same
   158	unconditional divisor representer. -/
   159	def affineGenusChart {ι : Type u}
   160	    (m : ι → ℕ) (Z : ι → (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
   161	    (hdeg : ∀ i, Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k (Z i)
   162	      = (m i : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (genus C : ℤ))
   163	    (V : ∀ _ : ι, (divRepAffGenusScheme C).left.Opens) (i : ι) :
   164	    yoneda.obj (V i : Scheme) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1 :=
   165	  restrictChart (abelSigmaChartAffGenus C (m i) (Z i) (hdeg i)) (V i)
   166	
   167	/-- The structure morphism of a restricted genus chart is the inclusion of its source open
   168	followed by the structure morphism of the chosen divisor representer. -/
   169	lemma chartHom_affineGenusChart {ι : Type u}
   170	    (m : ι → ℕ) (Z : ι → (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
   171	    (hdeg : ∀ i, Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k (Z i)
   172	      = (m i : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (genus C : ℤ))
   173	    (V : ∀ _ : ι, (divRepAffGenusScheme C).left.Opens) (i : ι) :
   174	    chartHom C (affineGenusChart C m Z hdeg V) i
   175	      = (V i).ι ≫ (divRepAffGenusScheme C).hom := by
   176	  have hrestrict := chartHom_restrictChart (C := C)
   177	    (abelSigmaChartAffGenus C (m i) (Z i) (hdeg i)) (V i) i
   178	  have hgenus := chartHom_abelSigmaChartAffGenus C (m i) (Z i) (hdeg i) i
   179	  simpa only [chartHom, affineGenusChart] using
   180	    hrestrict.trans (congrArg ((V i).ι ≫ ·) hgenus)

   182	/-- The degree-zero Picard functor is represented by the glued object of any pointwise-covering
   183	family of open genus-parameter widened Abel charts.
   184	
   185	The divisor representation is construction data, not a hypothesis: it is supplied by
   186	`divFunctorAff_genus_representableBy`.  The two hypotheses are exactly the geometric inputs of
   187	Zariski local representability. -/
   188	def pic0RepresentableByOfAffineGenusCharts {ι : Type u}
   189	    (m : ι → ℕ) (Z : ι → (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
   190	    (hdeg : ∀ i, Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k (Z i)
   191	      = (m i : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (genus C : ℤ))
   192	    (V : ∀ _ : ι, (divRepAffGenusScheme C).left.Opens)
   193	    (hf : ∀ i, IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (affineGenusChart C m Z hdeg V i))
   194	    (hcov : PointwiseCoverage C (affineGenusChart C m Z hdeg V)) :
   195	    Σ J : Over (Spec (.of k)), (pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy J := by
   196	  letI : Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology
   197	      (Sigma.desc (affineGenusChart C m Z hdeg V)) :=
   198	    isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc_of_pointwise C _ hcov
   199	  exact ⟨_, pic0RepresentableByOfCharts C (affineGenusChart C m Z hdeg V) hf⟩

    13	gluing keystone (§8.6), and finally a functor `divFunctorAff` with a natural transformation
    14	`divFunctorToAff` out of the chart-typed one (ADDENDUM 9).  What it did **not** have, at every
    15	one of those milestones, is a **consumer**: measured at HEAD, the widened names appeared in zero
    16	files outside the `Picard/DivisorFamilyAff*.lean` family.
    17	
    18	That is the gap this file closes.  It restates the DD-R general-test pullback
    19	(`DivRepAffinePullback.pullGlobal`, `Picard/DivRepGlobalLift.lean`) on the widened functor and
    20	proves the `pull_comp` law there — the one field of `DivRepGlobalData` that is *about* the
    21	functor rather than about a single test.

    23	## What the restatement costs, and why that is the point
    24	
    25	Nothing but a push-forward.  `pullGlobalAff` is `divFamZarToAffVehicle ∘ pullGlobal`, and its
    26	naturality is the chart-typed `pullGlobal_comp` transported along `divFamZarToAffVehicle_map`.
    27	No gluing is redone and no certificate is re-derived over a widened cover.
    28	
    29	That cheapness is the substantive claim: it says the widened layer is *usable* by the existing
    30	DD-R stack, not merely well-formed.  A functor nothing consumes and a functor everything can
    31	consume look identical to a sorry census and to a job count.

    33	## Direction, once more
    34	
    35	Old → new.  A consumer that already produces a chart-typed section gets its widened counterpart

    37	ADDENDUM 4 §4.3 a straddling divisor at genus `≥ 2` is confined by no fixed pair of `P¹` charts.
    38	So this file does **not** claim the widened functor is representable by `DivOver`; it claims the
    39	chart-typed representability datum pushes forward to a compatible family of widened values.

    10	# cert-assemble on the widened cover: from a straddling piece to `DivFamZarAff`
    11	
    12	Roadmap leaf `AJCR.w4-rep.datum.dat-d.ddr.certificate.cert-assemble`, over the widened
    13	predicate.  This composes the lane into one statement: **pointwise on the base, a straddling
    14	affine piece plus the (c1)/(c2) inputs give a widened locally-certified system**, hence a
    15	`DivFamZarAff` class.
    16	
    17	## What each hypothesis is, and why it is where it is
    18	
    19	The assembler takes, at each prime `p` of the base, an away localization `r ∉ p` over which:
    20	
    21	* the pulled system has an adaptation whose cover has a **straddling piece**
    22	  (`SwallowedBy`) — the Stacks `0B8B` geometric input, explicit per I-0492 clause 2;
    23	* the **glued clauses** (c2)/(c3)/(c4) hold.  These are not free **in general**:
    24	  `cert-collapse` showed the diagonal of the difference arrow vanishes identically, so (c4)
    25	  always forces flatness of the diagonal overlap colengths (I-0340).  That refutation stands
    26	  and is about an ARBITRARY adaptation.  **But under `SwallowedBy` — which this assembler
    27	  already assumes — they are derivable rather than assumed**: `ovlColengthDiagEquiv`
    28	  (`…AffGlue.lean`) identifies `ovlColength i i` with `colength i`, so the flatness (c4)
    29	  forces *is* (c1)-flatness, and `AffAdaptation.isCertified_of_swallowedBy_of_c1` delivers all
    30	  seven clauses from (c1) plus the rank datum with these five hypotheses gone.  This
    31	  five-hypothesis form is kept because it survives for covers that are **not** swallowed;
    32	  a caller on a straddling cover should prefer the derived form (I-0668);
    33	* the **fibrewise-regularity** input for (c1)-projectivity, which is I-0492 clause 4(i) in
    34	  its per-piece form.  It is a hypothesis, not carrier data.
    35	
    36	The clauses (c1) themselves are *produced*, not assumed: `finite_colength` from the
    37	straddling piece via the support-trace engine, `projective_colength` from the fibrewise
    38	input via the widened flatness route.  That is the whole value the lane adds — clause (c1),
    39	the one the fixed-pair design could not supply for a straddling divisor, now comes for free
    40	from an affine-open cover.
    41

    43	
    44	* `AffAdaptation.isCertified_of_swallowedBy` — the certificate from a straddling piece plus
    45	  the glued clauses and the fibrewise input.
    46	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isLocallyCertifiedAff_of_forall_prime_swallowed` — the pointwise
    47	  assembler.
    48	* `AlgebraicGeometry.divFamZarAff_of_forall_prime_swallowed` — the resulting class, the

   286	/-! ## Non-vacuity, and the exact strength of the witness
   287	
   288	Trap (c) of the workspace probe catalogue (`I-0442`): a theorem whose hypotheses cannot hold
   289	jointly is vacuously true and reports clean axioms like any other, so `#print axioms` on the gate
   290	says nothing about whether it is about anything.  The inhabitation is therefore exhibited.
   291	
   292	**The caveat is inherited and must be stated here rather than only upstream.**  The gate's
   293	hypotheses are exactly the endpoint's, so the endpoint's witness inhabits them — and that witness
   294	sits at `n = 0` with an EMPTY support locus (`exists_isCertified_of_seed_of_supportLocus_empty`,
   295	`…AffSeedEndpoint.lean`).  Its own scope paragraph says what it is worth, and the same reading
   296	applies verbatim to the gate: it rules out the hypotheses contradicting each other outright, and
   297	it does **not** rule out the weaker-but-real possibility that they hold only at `n = 0`.  Read the
   298	lemma below as *"the gate is not about nothing"*, never as *"the gate is non-trivially
   299	inhabited"*.
   300	
   301	What is known about `n > 0` is unchanged by this file: the gate fires whenever the degree datum is
   302	supplied at that `n`, and nothing in the hypothesis set forces `n = 0`; supplying that datum from
   303	geometry at a specific `n > 0` is the seed layer's business.  The genuinely non-vacuous witness
   304	would need a straddling divisor, which exists over every field (spec ADDENDUM 4 §4.3) but is out
   305	of scope to formalise (§4.5 — it needs `Sym^g C`).  Cf. `DivisorFamilyAffStrict.lean`, whose
   306	strictness theorem carries the identical caveat for the identical reason. -/
   307	
   308	/-- **The gate's hypothesis set is jointly inhabited**, at the zero divisor with `n = 0`: the
   309	support locus is empty, so the `0B8B` containment holds for any affine open inside a cover member
   310	and every colength vanishes.

   114	/-! ## The forward half -/
   115	
   116	variable (C π) in
   117	/-- **The forward half of `IsChartDatumPresentation`, pointwise.**
   118	
   119	If the datum presents `μ` at `κ(t)` as plus classes (`IsChartDatumPlusFibre`, which mentions no
   120	witness), then the datum's fibre predicate at `κ(t)` implies the split predicate for `μ`'s fibre.
   121	
   122	The proof is the **trivial splitting**: take `L := κ(t)`, the identity extension.  The witness
   123	divisor the datum predicate hands over already lies in the right class and already has vanishing
   124	`H¹`, so nothing has to be transported.  `isSplitWitness_of_presenting_witness_self` is the
   125	instance of the introduction rule this needs, and it is the instance memory I-0564 recorded as
   126	unelaborable — see its docstring in `Picard/Pic0ChartTwistSplit.lean` for why staging the
   127	existentials makes it a one-liner.
   128	
   129	Note what this does *not* need: no separability argument, no common refinement, no descent.  All
   130	of that belongs to the converse. -/
   131	theorem isSplitWitness_of_hasWitnessH1Vanishing {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
   132	    {μ : picEt C (overSpec k A)} {D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C A π}
   133	    (hfib : IsChartDatumPlusFibre C π μ D) (t : (overSpec k A).left)
   134	    (h : D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t)) :
   135	    IsSplitWitness C (picEtMap C (Over.testPoint t) μ) := by
   136	  obtain ⟨W, hW, hW1⟩ := h
   137	  exact isSplitWitness_of_presenting_witness_self C _ _ (hfib t) W hW hW1
   138	
   139	/-! ## The `↔`, with the owed direction named -/
   140	
   141	variable (C π) in
   142	/-- **`IsChartDatumPresentation` assembled** — the forward half proved, the converse named.
   143	
   144	Stated so that a lane closing CHART-U(b) sees exactly one obligation rather than two: given the
   145	witness-free plus-class identity, the `→` direction is free, and what remains is `hconv`.
   146	
   147	`hconv` is the descent direction: from a split witness over *some* extension `L_t/κ(t)` chosen
   148	per point, produce the datum's predicate at `κ(t)` itself.  Its two ingredients both exist —
   149	`hasWitnessH1Vanishing_iff_of_fieldExtension` carries a *datum* predicate across a field
   150	extension, and `hfib` identifies the classes — but composing them is not a rewrite, because the
   151	witness received lies in `μ`'s class at `L_t` rather than visibly in `D`'s at `κ(t)`.
   152	
   153	**`hconv` IS DISCHARGED as of 2026-07-29** (`Picard/Pic0ChartPresentationConverse.lean`,
   154	`hasWitnessH1Vanishing_of_isSplitWitness_at`), and the diagnosis above was right about the
   155	obstruction while **naming only two of the three ingredients**.  The step that makes the
   156	received witness *visibly* lie in `D`'s class is not a transport at all: it is
   157	`PicEtAff.unit_injective` (`Picard/CechKernelLemma.lean:361`, Kleiman 2.5(1), the unconditional
   158	close of the ζ3 campaign) followed by `relPicMk_injective_of_subsingleton`, which together force
   159	the presenting class `M` to *equal* `D`'s fibre class at `L_t`.  Then
   160	`hasWitnessH1Vanishing_iff_of_fieldExtension` descends it, exactly as predicted.
   161	
   162	What the discharge consumes in place of `hconv` is the same plus-class identity as `hfib` but at
   163	an arbitrary extension of `κ(t)` (`IsChartDatumPlusFibreAt`); at `L := κ(t)` it *is* `hfib` by
   164	`Iff.rfl`.  So use `isChartDatumPresentation_of_plusFibre` rather than supplying `hconv` by
   165	hand — this theorem remains correct and is the general form. -/
   166	theorem isChartDatumPresentation_of_plusFibre_of_converse {A : Type u} [CommRing A]
   167	    [Algebra k A] {μ : picEt C (overSpec k A)} {D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C A π}
   168	    (hfib : IsChartDatumPlusFibre C π μ D)
   169	    (hconv : ∀ t : (overSpec k A).left,
   170	      IsSplitWitness C (picEtMap C (Over.testPoint t) μ) →
   171	        D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t)) :
   172	    IsChartDatumPresentation C π μ D :=
   173	  fun t => ⟨isSplitWitness_of_hasWitnessH1Vanishing C π hfib t, hconv t⟩

    12	Continuation of `AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivSchemeCertificate` (the 500-line cap forced

    18	* `DivisorAdaptation.gluedEquivVanishing` — **the junction equivalence**
